articleTitle: Comparison between Frequency Selective Surfaces with Rectangular and Hexagonal Periodicity Operating as Absorbers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Two frequency selective surfaces operating as absorbers, with rectangular and hexagonal periodicity respectively, and relying on the same metal pattern in the unit cell are compared. The structures are implemented on an FR4 substrate, covered with copper metallization. The frequency responses (reflection coefficient) in normal incidence of electromagnetic waves and contents of higher order modes in the two cases are compared. Finally, the frequency response in oblique incidence of the hexagonal array is reported.

articleTitle: Quantum Computational Electromagnetics—Recent Progress
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Classical computational electromagnetics (CEM) has seen leaps and bounds progress since the 1960’s, shortly after the advent of the digital computer. As a result, this knowledge has transformed how classical electromagnetics engineering has been performed. Virtual prototyping using CEM is routine in many areas of technology development related to classical electromagnetics. After over 50 years of development, a healthy knowledge base has been grown that many practitioners in the field can rely on. It thus presages a similar knowledge base for quantum electromagnetics, which is an emerging field of growing importance. This knowledge base is instrumental for the growth and success of many quantum technologies including quantum computing, sensing, communications, encryption, imaging, and metrology.

articleTitle: Evaluating the velocity of ships from low-resolution SAR images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is a fundamental tool in maritime surveillance for its weather and daylight insensitivity and large swath. Position, size and bearing of a target ship can be extracted with high accuracy from a SAR image. Additionally, those images contain several cues to estimate the target velocity. However, dealing with spatial resolutions of tens of meters, the applicability of some approaches is questionable. We formerly experimented two velocity estimation methods based on the features extracted from the wake of a sailing ship [1]: one is based on the wavelength of the cusp waves characterizing the Kelvin wake pattern; the other is based on the typical azimuth shift that affects moving targets imaged by a SAR system. Both methods directly return the radial component of the ship speed; the azimuthal speed, and thus the complete velocity vector, can finally be reconstructed using the estimated ship track. The mentioned techniques rely on the detection of significant parts of the wake in the SAR image. This is not always possible, especially with low-resolution images, due to a combination of unfavorable incidence angles and rough status of the sea.

articleTitle: An Analysis of The NASA CSDA Bistatic Radar GNSS-R Dataset
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The remote sensing of the Earth’s surface through a variety of spaceborne platforms has a long history of investigation. The selection of one sensing technology over another is typically governed by the geophysical products of interest and requirements of spatial and temporal sampling. Recent studies have highlighted the utility of GNSS-R (Global Navigation Satellite System-Reflectometry) measurements for the sensing of multiple geophysical properties. The modest cost of GNSS-R receive-only platforms also promotes the simultaneous launch of multiple receivers, further improving revisit times, and the L-band frequency used provides all weather operations given the insensitivity of L-band measurements to cloud cover and even heavy rain rates.

articleTitle: 3D-Printing of All-Dielectric Electromagnetic Devices: Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The rapid advancement of three-dimensional printing (3DP) technology has opened up new possibilities for fabricating novel functional structures with electromagnetic (EM) properties. Materials with high dielectric permittivity are of significant interest in 3D printing of devices for advanced electromagnetic applications due to their ability to enhance device performance, enable miniaturization and compact designs, offer customization and tailored properties, and provide design freedom. High dielectric permittivity materials enhance the performance of EM devices by enabling efficient energy storage and manipulation of electric fields, leading to improved functionality and increased signal processing capabilities. Furthermore, 3DP enables the fabrication of complex geometries and customized structures, and incorporating materials with high dielectric permittivity provides precise control over the electromagnetic properties, enabling the realization of advanced functionalities and designs.

articleTitle: An Ultra-wideband Feed Horn for the Green Bank Telescope
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: An ultra-wideband feed horn is designed and fabricated in the frequency range 0.7 to 4 GHz. The scientific goals are to improve pulsar timing observations by allowing continuous coverage of the band. Given the GBT optics, mechanical limitations constrain the optimization of the maximum aperture efficiency to minimum system noise temperature ratio. To achieve these goals a quad-ridge design is selected. A technique is developed for the manufacture of a low loss vacuum window with adequate strength and low permeability. Measurements of the far field patterns, noise temperature and GBT system equivalent flux density are compared to model-based predictions. Modifications of the ridge profiles to control the modal content and improve efficiency are explored.

articleTitle: The Evolution of Chorus Emissions Over Time and Magnetic Latitude
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Chorus wave emissions are pervasive electromagnetic waves observed throughout the inner magnetosphere, and can intensify significantly during enhanced geomagnetic activity. Chorus waves have been shown to drive a particular type of precipitation that is composed of ring current and radiation belt losses and results in the quasi-periodic optical ionospheric phenomenon called pulsating aurora. Understanding how chorus waves evolve over time following periods of generation and rapid growth (i.e. injection-driven) and how they evolve as they propagate from equatorial sources to higher magnetic latitudes will lead to insights about how they drive energetic electron precipitation.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Planar Ultra-Wideband Phased Array Antenna with FSS Superstrate Loading
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A low-profile planar ultra-wideband phased array antenna is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna element adopts a dual-polarized topology and utilizes two orthogonal polarized printed dipoles as radiation structures. To achieve better scanning ability, the wide-angle impedance matching (WAIM) layers consisting of the frequency selective surface (FSS) superstrate are loaded above the dipole patches, and the parasitic metal strips are introduced and placed below for a lower profile. The sizes of the proposed antenna element are $0.5\times 0.5\lambda_{high^{2}}$($\lambda_{high}$ is the free-space wavelength at the highest operating frequency), and the profile is only 0.228$\lambda_{high}$. Calculated results show that the active VSWRs of the proposed infinite array are below 2.9 at broadside radiation and scanning to ± 60° in the E/H planes within 2-6 GHz. Meanwhile, the isolations between orthogonal ports are mostly greater than 20dB. To verify the proposed designs, an array prototype is fabricated and measured. The measured results are in an acceptable agreement with the calculated ones.

articleTitle: Chaotic dynamics of electromagnetic field in plane-parallel resonator with semitransparent nonlinear layer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A plane-parallel resonator, containing a thin translucent layer of active or passive material with a nonlinear dependence of the current density (magnetic moment) on the electric (magnetic) field, can be considered as the simplest model of many electronic devices in the microwave, terahertz, and optical frequency ranges. Very often the nonlinear layer has its size along the wave propagation direction much smaller of the oscillation’s wavelength. It may be placed either at the resonator wall, or at the arbitrary point inside the resonator. In this case the nonlinear transformation of the resonator partial waves by the active element takes place, and the spatial-temporal dynamics of the field may be either a simple standing wave or become a very complicate nonlinear, but still deterministic dynamics. Finally, the field dynamics may be a stochastic one. These processes are very convenient to describe within the frame of the approach proposed in [1, 2] and developed in later publications, e.g. [3]. The main idea of that approach consists in accounting the nonlinear field-current interaction in the boundary conditions, but not in the wave equations. Introducing Reimann invariants for electromagnetic field components of plane waves in the resonator, and using their invariance on the wave equation characteristics one may reduce the primary complicated initial-boundary value problem for partial differential equations with nonlinear boundary conditions to the much simpler mathematical object - nonlinear difference or difference-differential equation, or to the set of such equations for the one of the field components (or on the several ones). This simplification enables to carry on an efficient analysis of spatial-temporal dynamics of electromagnetic field in case of self-oscillatory active devices or in resonant systems with passive nonlinear thin inserts, etc. In the paper, the common statement of the problems is formulated for the case of the surface with the set of lamped active elements and also for passive semitransparent layer, such as semiconductor or ferromagnetic metasurfaces [4]. Solutions for the obtained equations of self-oscillations in the resonator with the active layer placed at 1/3 of the resonator length are shown in Figure 1: we observe relaxation oscillations for a small parameter of nonlinearity and for strong nonlinearity we observe chaos

articleTitle: General Method of Moment for Solving the Surface Integral Equation Using the Green’s Function Calculator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Method of Moment (MoM) applied to Surface Integral Equations (SIEs) represents one of the most efective methods for full wave analysis of composite metallic and dielectric structures in the frequency domain [1]. In general case composite metallic and dielectric structures consist of domains made of homogeneous, linear and isotropic materials. SIEs for such structures uses surface equivalence principle to decompose n-domain problem into n single domain problems, mutually coupled by surface equivalent currents (electric and magnetic), and appropriate boundary condtions. In this way evaluation of EM fields due to equivalent currents is based on simple free space Green functions. Implementation of higher order bases augmented with parallelization on CPU and GPU enable solution of complex multi-scale problems at powerful desktop machines (maximum dimension up to 1000 wavelengths, maximum number of unknowns up to one million) [2].

articleTitle: Application of the Method of Moments in Telescope Coronagraph Pupil and Focal Plane Mask Design
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Since its founding, NASA has been consistently working to discover habitable exoplanets, which are Earth-like planets outside the solar system, usually orbiting another star. To determine whether an exoplanet is habitable or not, it is desirable to take a direct image of it. Unfortunately, this is an extremely challenging task. If the solar system were observed from 10 parsecs, which is about 32.6 light-years, away, the Earth is within 0.1 arcsec from the Sun and is about 10 billion times dimmer. The extraordinarily small angular separation between an exoplanet and its host star and the extremely weak exoplanet light make the direct observation of the exoplanet next to impossible. To battle such a challenge and search for Earth-size exoplanet, the direct starlight suppression at a small angular separation is the key capability and coronagraphy is a major approach to achieving such a capability.

articleTitle: Volume-Surface Integral Equation Solver For Chiral Media
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A volume-surface integral equation solver is pro-posed to solve the transmission problem for systems containing domains occupied by chiral media. Homogeneous domains can be modelled by boundary element methods and inhomogenous regions can be modelled by volume element methods, resulting in a minimal number of degrees of freedom to describe the problem. This is achieved by introducing surface current densities on the boundary and contrast current densities in the bulk of the domain. The electric and magnetic fields are used as volumetric unknowns. Results for scattering by a chiral sphere are compared to the Mie-series solution, demonstrating the method’s accuracy.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study of Optimized Metasurface Matching Layer in Near Field
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Electromagnetic devices often require the maximization of the transmitted field, especially for biomedical applications. The employment of a matching layer can reduce the reflections at the air/skin interface, but it is often realized without design guidelines and it may result bulky. On the other hand, introducing a metasurface can improve user’s comfort. A rigorous procedure to find the parameters of the matching layer, also comprising the metasurface, can help in its design. Here, we extend the analytical optimization procedure of our previous works by considering a real patch antenna instead of a short dipole. An experimental setup for retrieving the electric field inside a tissue-mimicking phantom is also presented. Three cases are considered: no matching layer, dielectric-only matching layer and metasurface matching layer. The preliminary results show a good agreements with the theoretical ones.

articleTitle: Broadband, Full-Duplex Transceive Amplifier for Bi-Static, Reflectometer-Operated Radar Applications in X-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper introduces and investigates several full-duplex components for the realization of Bi-static Radar operation driven by commercial one port reflectometers. Next to the component requirements, two broadband transceive (TRX) amplifier concepts are presented. The introduced topologies are investigated and optimized in simulations. Measurement results and performance of the manufactured components are discussed in detail and are compared to already existing realizations.

articleTitle: Sensor Design for mm-Wave In Vitro Epithelial Cell Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Single cells or a bulk of cells are already electrically characterized below 40 GHz with standard methods. They can be classified as dead or alive, usually while trapped in a closed microfluidic chamber surrounded by microstrip lines [1–2]. These methods can’t be applied to epithelial cells, which can be found in the lung and are responsible for the gas exchange and therefore are important for research on the human physiology. This is because the cells have liquid, in form of blood, on one side and air on the other side. Drowning them in a microfluidic system will put the cells under stress, which influences the measurement. Additionally, methods focusing on single cells are not suitable, since the function of the whole cell layer is neglected.

articleTitle: Performance of the Normally-Integrated Magnetic Field Integral Equation for Fla Faceted Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The “normally-integrated” magnetic field integral equation (NIMFIE) formulation was introduced in [1] and used to analyze scattering from toroidal targets in [2]. The traditional MFIE has several limitations that the NIMFIE approach attempts to ameliorate. By incorporating integrals in directions that are both tangential and normal to the target surface, the NIMFIE formulation produces a true “weak” form of the MFIE where all derivatives are absorbed by testing integrals. In [1–2] the approach was used to simplify the matrix entry calculations associated with higher order representations and curved models of surfaces. It was demonstrated in [1] that the approach is easily modified to enable it to suppress internal resonances. Although one of the limitations of the traditional MFIE is that it can become unstable when applied to a multiply-connected geometry [3–4], the NIMFIE approach was shown to be stable for thick and thin loop targets [2]. The primary limitation of the NIMFIE formulation is shared with the traditional MFIE: targets under investigation must be closed bodies that are not too electrically thin (since one of the testing integrals follows a path into the target).

articleTitle: Time-switched metasurfaces: Conversion from guided to radiated modes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In recent years, several novel and interesting wave phenomena emerging from the class of artificial engineerable materials and surfaces with time-varying properties have been identified and studied [1–3]. Many researchers have proposed innovative devices able to manipulate the electromagnetic radiation, enabling impedance-matching in time domain [4–5], energy harvesting [6–8] and analog computing [9].

articleTitle: Characterizing surface phonon polaritons in quartz by near-field microscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Surface phonon polaritons (SPhPs) are hybrid light-matter states originating from strong coupling between photons and optical phonons which are quasiparticles of lattice vibration. SPhP can be excited in the strong reflection bands in the infrared (IR) region (Reststrahlen region) of polar crystal, where the real part of the dielectric constant is negative. Control of SPhP is expected to be one of the promising ways to improve the thermal conductivity of nanoscale devices because the propagation length of SPhP is as long as $100 \mu m. SiC [1]$ and quartz [2, 3] are polar crystals that are often used for SPhP excitation. Due to crystal lattice vibrations inherent in a quartz [2], the reflectivity of a quartz is significantly decreased at around $1160 cm^{-1}$, although these frequencies are within Reststrahlen region. In the previous work, SPhP excitation was not observed at around $1160 cm^{-1}$ in the attenuated total reflection (ATR) spectrum [3]. For further understanding of the fundamental characteristics of SPhP in a quartz, the direct visualization of SPhP in real space is crucial. In this work, we investigated the frequency dependence of SPhP propagation on a quartz surface by using the scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy ($s -$SNOM), which enables nanoscale spectroscopic imaging [1].

articleTitle: Recent Advances on Multi-Scale Wave Manipulation through Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The vision of Smart ElectroMagnetic Environment (SEME) has emerged in the last few years as a fundamental approach for the development of next generation wireless systems capable of delivering the required quality-of-service in comparison with current-generation architectures [1]–[5]. In fact, SEME aims at addressing the fundamental challenges arising in wireless communications and sensing by fixed propagation environments, which are traditionally considered an uncontrollable component that can only be compensated for by using increasingly sophisticated transmission/reception techniques as well as more expensive designs / higher power levels [1]–[5]. More in detail, SEME is based on a revolutionary approach to wireless system design in which the wave propagation and its interactions with existing “obstacles” can be “manipulated” to properly adapt the resulting end-to-end electromagnetic scenario to the designer’s needs and the system-level requirements and performance goals.

articleTitle: Advanced Wave Manipulation for Smart EM Environment through Static Passive Skins
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The possibility to manipulate the propagation of waves through two-dimensional inexpensive devices installed opportunistically is one of the cornerstones of the Smart Electromagnetic Environment (SEME) vision. As a matter of fact, the availability of such technology opens the path to a wide range of opportunities for wireless network designers in terms of coverage improvement, obstacle bypassing, signal-to-noise-ratio enhancement, and quality-of-service upgrade without the need of installing new base stations or access points. Such an innovative paradigm in wireless systems design and planning has gathered a lot of attention both from the academic and from the industrial viewpoint owing to its potentialities in terms of energy efficiency and reduction of radio-frequency emission, scalability, and cost mitigation when introducing innovative services.

articleTitle: On the equivalence of coupled resonators and Yee cells
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The circuit of coupled resonators can be used to solve electromagnetic problems. The paper present conditions to obtain equivalence of the coupled resonator circuits and the circuit representations of Yee cells. The resonators resonant frequency is related to the size of Yee cell. The coupling between resonators is maximum i.e. equal to 1. The type of coupling is magnetic. To realize equivalent circuits the recently introduced frequency dependent inverter is used.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable and time modulated metasurfaces enabling a new generation of smart antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Time-modulated and reconfigurable metasurfaces, i.e. the third generation of electromagnetic metasurfaces [1], enable an unprecedented control of the electromagnetic field [2]–[4]. Their properties can be applied successfully in the development of future smart radio environments, as intelligent reflectors manipulating and routing signals in the desired directions. At the same time, time-modulated and reconfigurable metasurfaces can be paired with regular antennas and antenna arrays, in the form of meta-covers or meta-domes, to conceive a new generation of smart antennas, whose intelligence is brought by the intelligent hardware of the metasurfaces, rather than by the signal processing modules. This solution makes the overall antenna systems less complex and capable of handling and processing an ever more significant amount of data, avoiding i. down-conversion from the electromagnetic frequency to the baseband, ii. analog-to-digital conversion, iii. implementation of beamforming, modulation/demodulation, and data extraction schemes through proper algorithms, and iv. the whole chain back to the radio link (digital-to-analog conversion, up-conversion from the baseband to the electromagnetic frequency). Antennas based on these concepts can be cognitive – being able to scan the electromagnetic environments, check for possible interferences (both in terms of frequencies and angular directions), and self-adjust its properties (e.g. operation frequency, radiation pattern, polarization, visibility-invisibility mode) accordingly – and are perfect candidates for joint communication and sensing.

articleTitle: Development and Applications of the Laplacian Representation Approach for the Asymptotic Part of the Layered-Medium Green’s Function in the Mixed Potential Formulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We report on developments in the evaluation of matrix elements of the electric and magnetic field operators involving the asymptotic (large transverse wave-number or small transverse distances) components of the mixed-potential Green’s function of a layered medium. Subtracting these asymptotic terms significantly accelerates numerical computation of the Sommerfeld-type integrals required in constructing Green’s function and then x elements [1]. The described method is applicable to planar conducting structures embedded in a multi-layered medium. Ability of a fast and accurate evaluation of matrix elements for such structures is critical in many applications, especially in solving forward problems in design and optimization of electromagnetic metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Low-Profile 3D Printed Transmit-array for Wide-Angle Beam Scanning at Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Low-cost and compact antennas for wide-angle beam scanning in the mm-Wave band play a key role in the development of the next generation of terrestrial and satellite communication systems. Phased array antennas are currently getting a lot of attention for their excellent scanning with a low profile and mature manufacturing process [1]. However, the power consumption and losses due to their complex feeding network and large count of active components are still their main drawbacks. Both issues are overcome using spatially fed antennas (SFA) such as reconfigurable reflectarray (RA) or transmitarray (TA) antennas. These solutions avoid the feeding network, and the beam scanning is obtained using power-efficient controlling elements (PIN, MEMs, Liquid Crystal, etc.) [2]. However, they are still more costly and complex than solutions based on passive periodic structures combined with mechanical scanning (mainly reflector-based antennas, RA, or TA).

articleTitle: An Analytical Solution to Investigate the Impact of an Insulating Layer with High Permittivity Materials in Magnetic Resonance Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this work we present a new analytical framework to investigate how the presence of an insulating layer, such as the distance between a high-permittivity helmet and the body tissues can impact the field distribution in the region of interest, and the choice of the optimum permittivity to this purpose. The framework is based on a recent reformulation of the Mie scattering for a layered sphere and is validated with a numerical method based on the finite difference time domain.

articleTitle: Analytical evaluation of the 4-D singular integral: a different perspective for a systematic approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Currently, one bottleneck of the Method of Moments is related to the fast and accurate computation of near-field interactions. These entail the evaluation of four dimensional integrals whose integrand may be singular. Only recently purely analytical solutions have been proposed in the literature. While showing great promises and being already competitive with state-of-the-art methods, these techniques are still perfectible, both in terms of formulation and implementation. In this paper, we build on a technique previously published by the authors and propose a different formulation. While being mathematically equivalent, the proposed formulation is conceptually more intuitive and flexible. The additional flexibility can be exploited to improve the formulation of the analytical solution, further accelerate its numerical implementation and reduce numerical noise arising from the finite double precision.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Ray Tracing Simulation and Imaging of Complex Indoor Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Indoor imaging scenarios involving complex environments are studied by utilizing a combination of ray tracing and imaging algorithms. The utilized ray tracer is based on computing equivalent sources on a Huygens surface, which can be placed arbitrarily between the antennas and the considered scattering objects. To verify the simulation results we compute synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images for several configurations by utilizing an inverse source based reconstruction algorithm and compare the results to those obtained by a standard backprojection algorithm.

articleTitle: Microsecond electric pulses effects in spinal cord injuries: results from RISEUP project
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Spinal Cord Injury (SCI), a major cause of paralysis, currently has no effective therapies. Every year almost 500.000 people are diagnosed with SCI worldwide. he difficulty on the neuronal restoration after SCI is based on the complex cascade of events that inexorably cause a degenerative chronic stage mainly favored by the non-permissive environment and limited capacity for axonal regrowth. RISEUP, an Europen project, proposes to attain neuronal functional regeneration after SCI by an unprecedented and unique bio-hybrid-compatible electro-activated and wireless rechargeable implantable technology. RISEUP introduces high voltage microsecond electric pulses stimulations and low amplitude direct currents on a combination of stem cells, induced neural stem cells (iNSCs) and multipotent stromal cells (MSCs), whose transplantation is facilitated by an innovative scaffold biomaterial (Fig.1).

articleTitle: Space debris Identification and Tracking (SINTRA)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The SINTRA program aims to investigate the interaction of orbital debris with the surrounding space environment and drive the state of the art to detect, track, and characterize lethal non-trackable orbital space debris. Space debris poses a significant risk to all space missions. With an average low Earth orbit (LEO) impact velocity of 22,500 MPH, even the smallest of debris can cause significant damage. [1] Currently, there are over 100 million objects greater than 1 mm orbiting the Earth, [2, 3] however, less than 1 percent of debris that can cause mission-ending damage are currently tracked. [4] Due to the dynamic nature of the near-Earth space environment, predicting the trajectory of the debris is extremely difficult necessitating persistent monitoring. [5] While debris larger than 10 cm can be detected and tracked, smaller debris cannot be tracked using current capabilities. [6] Therefore, there is an increased interest in tracking debris less than 10 cm. The detection, tracking, and characterization of lethal non-trackable space debris would support the safe operation of valuable space assets worldwide.

articleTitle: Investigation of detection range for bedsores using electromagnetic waves
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Bedsores are injuries caused by pressure on the skin for a long time and obstruction of blood flow. As the damage progresses, the treatment period becomes longer. In some cases, patients require surgery. So early detection is essential. In this study, we develop a noncontact bedsores detection system using electromagnetic waves at 10.5 GHz.In this report, we investigated the detectable range in bedsores detection.

articleTitle: Plasma Sources and Diagnostic Solution for Investigating Laboratory Plasmas
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Laboratory plasma experiments serve as an essential tool for mimicking complicated phenomena seen in space plasma and at the plasma-material interface encountered in industrial and fusion applications. The plasma parameter for the aforementioned medium typically ranges from extremely low densities (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> particles m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>) to as high as n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf> >10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup> m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, and the electron temperatures typically fall in the range of a few eV to as high as 10 eV. The formation of a quasi-neutral plasma with electrons and positive ions or a mixture of three species made up of electrons, positive ions, and negative ions will depend on the type of gas (electropositive or electronegative) utilised to generate the plasma. It is not only a pressing issue, but also necessitates accurate plasma diagnostics to create a variety of plasma conditions in laboratories. Creating a diverse plasma conditions in laboratories is not only an imminent challenge, but also requires reliable plasma diagnostics to characterize them. External parameters such as confinement of plasma using magnetic field adds further complexity in the discharges. The mechanism used to create these plasmas, as well as the wall boundary conditions, have a substantial impact on their equilibrium properties [1, 2]. To improve these system’s performances and evaluate the experiment’s findings, fundamental understanding of how they work is essentially required.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Based Sensor Using Fractal Hilbert Structure for Liquid Characterization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this work, a simple and efficient approach is presented to design a metamaterial based sensitive sensor for liquid characterization. The proposed sensor based on the Hilbert structure has a compacted size of $40\times 60\times 1.6 \mathrm{mm}^{3}$. The Hilbert curve is used to enhance the sensitivity of the sensor by increasing the interaction area with the sample tested. The simulation studies are carried out by using the Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Microwave Studio. The resonant frequency of the proposed sensor is about 0.46 GHz. The resonant frequency has shifted approximately 30 MHz after the receptacle is printed on the sensor surface. The proposed sensor has successfully detected different samples of liquids. The variations of the resonant frequency, scattering parameters, bandwidth and quality factor of different samples are discussed.

articleTitle: Research on EMI Simulation of Fuel Cell Vehicle Drive System Based on Ansys
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In order to cope with the increasingly prominent contradiction between fuel supply and demand and environmental pollution, the world ’s major automobile producing countries have taken the development of new energy vehicles as a national strategy. Compared with traditional vehicles, the electric drive system of new energy vehicles is composed of high-power power electronic devices, including power batteries, high-power DC/AC inverters, drive motors, and high-voltage cables connected to them. These power electronic devices will produce strong electromagnetic interference during operation, which may affect the stability of vehicle operation or the normal operation of other electronic devices around. In this paper, a fuel cell model is proposed to replace the ideal voltage source in traditional research to analyze the electromagnetic interference characteristics of the electric drive system in fuel cell vehicles. This research has theoretical and practical significance for analyzing the electromagnetic interference of fuel cell vehicles in the actual operating environment.

publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The high scanning rate and scanning linearity of leaky-wave antennas (LWA) have attracted a lot of attentions, since it can reduce both the occupation of electromagnetic spectrum resources and requirements of accuracy for transmitters and receivers, respectively [1]. articleTitle: Wave Particle interactions in the magnetosphere, a charged particle perspective: Observations, Instrumentation and Mission Concepts
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: It is well known that the terrestrial magnetosphere contains natural emissions in the form of plasma waves ranging from broad band emissions (e.g., plasmaspheric hiss) to discrete emissions (e.g., Electromagnetic Ion Cyclotron-EMIC-waves). These may be excited by external stimuli such as solarwind structures or terrrestrial source such as lightning [Helliwell, 1969]. Theses plasma waves interact with charged particles in the magnetospheric radiation belts causing these particles to be energized or loss by precipitation into the atmosphere (for reviews see Kanekal and Miyoshi 2021; Millan and Thorne, 2007; Thorne 2010).

articleTitle: A novel MultiResolution Preconditioner Including Piecewise Homogeneous Dielectric Objects
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: An extensive literature demonstrates the capabilities of the hierarchical quasi-Helmholtz decomposition multiresolution preconditioner both to address the breakdowns for the surface integral equations and to improve the convergence in multiscale problems, until now only applied to perfect electrical conductors. In this work we present a novel methodology based on this efficient preconditioner able to solve arbitrary complex geometries composed of piecewise homogeneous composite objects, that automatically satisfies the boundary conditions. To the authors’ knowledge, this is the first work where a multilevel quasi-Helmholtz decomposition is applied to objects with dielectric junctions without the need of a weak enforcement of the continuity or a number-of-unknown-reduction scheme. Numerical examples demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed approach for the solution of complex problems involving multiple materials (dielectric and conductors).

Author Keywords: electric and magnetic currents combined field integral equation (JMCFIE)

articleTitle: A non-conventional planar phased array based on the field equivalence principle for wide angle steering of Gaussian beams
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A non-conventional planar phased array (PA) for generation and steering of Gaussian electromagnetic (EM) beams (GB) is investigated in detail. It includes a new approach. The near field of an ideal virtual antenna (VA), which generates the desired Gaussian beam, is calculated on a displaced and tilted planar finite size reference aperture (RAP) which intercepts most of the near field of VA. By the Schelkunoff’s equivalence principle, the tangential components of $VA$ on the RAP (the signature of VA) radiates the same field as VA. The tilt angle of RAP with respect to the VA is the steering angle of the GB. The RAP is divided into rectangular subapertures (SAP), simulating the elements of a PA. The fields of VA at the center of SAP’s are used as the excitations of the microstrip antenna elements replacing SAP. The SAP separations can be comparable to or greater than a wavelength. A subarray method is developed for the suppression of grating lobes. The numerical results are presented to validate the concept.

articleTitle: Incoherent Scatter Radar Diagnostic Capabilities for Remotely Sensing Ionospheric Plasma Signatures Caused By Space Debris
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Radar remote sensing of the ionosphere using collective Thomson or incoherent scattering from the ionospheric plasma has been a workhorse of the ionospheric research community for more than 60 years [1]. Weak radar backscatter from free ionospheric electrons, electrostatically modified by accompanying ions, is detectable using large radar systems with power-aperture products in the megawatt-hectare class. Many of these radars operate or have operated using frequencies from lower VHF through L-band, with typical center frequencies in the UHF band. The primary thermal plasma wave modes observed in this technique are the narrow ion-acoustic resonance, accessible day and night, and the Langmuir mode resonance, created by the presence of photoelectrons from either the local or conjugate hemisphere. Langmuir resonance signatures are very weak compared to ion-acoustic signatures, and have an offset both above and below the radar transmission frequency which is dependent on the ambient plasma frequency, typically between 2 and 12 MHz in Earth’s. Langmuir resonance lines can be measured very accurately and are directly related to ionospheric electron density and temperature. Gyro line resonances were also occasionally observed using Arecibo and EISCAT VHF radars but are generally very weak and inaccessible to smaller instruments.

articleTitle: Second Order Transition Boundary Condition for not Dense Thin Sheets Analysis with MoM
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Impedance boundary conditions allow one to replace a complex structure with an appropriate impedance relationship between the electric and magnetic fields on the surface of the object. The interest in this topic has arisen many years ago to study the electromagnetic scattering from complex objects and continues since there are numerous electromagnetic applications in which it is necessary to analyze structures composed of dielectric sheets with small thicknesses in terms of wavelength.

articleTitle: Alternative Computational Techniques for the Numerical Analysis of Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The theory of characteristic modes (CM)has become extremely popular in the last 10 years.From the late 1960s (e.g., Garbacz 1968; Harrington et al., 1971) until now many advances have occurred.At its original form the electric field integral equation (EFIE) was used for the modal analysis of arbitrarily shaped perfect electric conductive (PEC) structures. For the case of dielectric and magnetic bodies a volume integral equation (VIE) formulationwas initially introduced. Although the VIE formulation was proven to be accurate, it requires a large number of unknowns when the electric size of the structure increases. To overcome this problem an equivalent surface integral equation (SIE) formulation was introduced in (Chang et al., 1977) which up to this day has dominated the field of characteristic mode analysis and several exceptional works have been proposed based on it (e.g., Yla-Oijala 2019).Despite the significance of all these works (see also the references in Yla-Oijala 2019), all theaforementioned CM techniques are based on method of moments (MoM), and they suffer from (a) inaccuracies as discussed in (e.g., Chen et al., 2015; Yla-Oijala 2019) and (b) several other issues related tounambiguous definitions of modes,tracking, and convergence. Here, we address the challenges traditional CM formulations have with the introduction of two alternative computational techniques. The first is a novel Green’s function-free characteristic modes formulation. Notably, our group was the first to propose this alternative CM formulation (e.g., Maximidis et al., 2012, Zekios et al., 2015, Paschaloudis et al., 2021] followed by others in the very recent years (e.g., Gustafsson et al,. 2022a; 2022b). Key advantage of the proposed formulation is that it does not require the evaluation of Green’sfunction, thereby the study of any arbitrarily shaped, multilayered geometry loaded with anisotropicand inhomogeneous materials is feasible. The second is a novel Green’s function formulation based on infinite ground plane Green’s functions. The key advantage of this formulation is its unique capability to identify only the real radiating modes over modes that appear as resonant (e.g., λ = 0) but in reality, they do not radiate despite the fact all traditional MoM formulations identify them as resonant with their eigenvalue λ = 0.

articleTitle: Design and Optimisation of a Double-Notch DQW HOM Coupler
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In accelerator physics, charged particles are accelerated to high energies using particle accelerators. A particle accelerator complex consists of several devices performing different functions. The radio-frequency (RF) cavity is a device that transfers electromagnetic energy generated by RF sources at the fundamental mode (FM) frequency to the charged particle bunches passing through the cavity. The electromagnetic field of the traversing, relativistic charged particles interacts with the cavity’s conductive wall. In that, off-axis particles excite higher-order modes (HOMs) in the cavity. Some HOMs propagate freely out of the cavity, while others are trapped. The high-impedance HOMs are potentially parasitic to beam stability and dynamics and, in some cases, could even lead to beam loss.

articleTitle: Leveraging Non-Hermitian Systems for Hardware Security in the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has resulted in an increasing number of information interactions among smart devices, including sensitive data that may be vulnerable to cyberattacks. Consequently, the need for robust cryptographic technologies with strong encryption capabilities has become critical. In this work, we propose a novel approach to address this demand by utilizing non-Hermitian systems as a hardware security primitive.

articleTitle: Maintenance-Free Wireless Sensor Networks for Infrastructure Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper proposes a solution for wireless monitoring of concrete structures using batteryless wireless sensor nodes based on UHF RFID technology. The system comprises a reader device and one or more wireless sensor nodes, which are connected to various sensors. The wireless sensor nodes are powered by the reader, and the communication protocol is based on ISO 18000-63. An external chloride sensor is used to gauge the concentration of chloride ions, which indicate the degree of corrosion of the concrete structure. The proposed system eliminates the need for cables or batteries and allows for data collection in hard-to-reach areas. To ensure reliable operation of the system, an automated antenna design methodology has been proposed that utilizes a pixelated structure based on a cross-shaped pattern. The methodology employs an evolutionary algorithm to generate an initial population of antenna designs, which are subjected to electromagnetic simulation using a commercial simulation tool. The performance of the sensor platform was evaluated in concrete blocks, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach for monitoring concrete structures.

articleTitle: Precipitation Curtains: Low-Altitude Footprint of Mesoscale Convection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Coupling of the solar wind and Earth’s magnetosphere is strongest during intervals of the southward interplanetary magnetic field (IMF), when magnetic reconnection at the subsolar magnetopause, with subsequent reconnection in the distant magnetotail, sets off a global convection cycle that transfers magnetic flux from the dayside into the magnetotail and then back to the dayside magnetosphere. Plasma sheet convection from the distant reconnection line to the inner magnetosphere exhibits a wide range of coupled multi-scale processes. Non-monotonic features in the plasma sheet magnetic terrain, such as minima, tailward gradients, or bumps in the northward component of the magnetic field lead to instabilities and energy transfer from large scale (~100 Earth radii) to mesoscale (~Earth radii) structures and earthward plasma flows. These in turn generate a wide range of kinetic scale (~100 km) phenomena which energize particles beyond 100 keV and produce bursts of particle precipitation into the atmosphere. In this paper we investigate the connection of energetic electron dynamics in mesoscale convection flows with electron precipitation into the atmosphere. We employ test-particle simulations in our Conservative Hamiltonian Integrator of Magnetospheric Particles (CHIMP) one way coupled to a high-resolution magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of plasma convection in the magnetotail. For the latter we use the Grid Agnostic MHD for Extended Research Applications (GAMERA) global magnetospheric model. We then use new modeling results and understanding of individual properties and impacts on plasmasheet dynamics to discuss Heliophysics Systems Observatory capabilities that would enable a system-wide view of cross-scale convection in Earth’s magnetotail. The paper analysis and discusses test particle simulation results (Figure 1) that show how electron transport and acceleration in complex magnetic terrain of mesoscale convection produce low-altitude footprint that resembles drifting precipitation structures known as “precipitation curtains”.

articleTitle: Laboratory studies of the coupling between dust, waves, and coherent plasma structures in the Magnetized Dusty Plasma Experiment (MDPX)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The presence of solid, charged particulate matter in plasmas, i.e., so-called “dusty” or “complex” plasmas, has been the subject of researchers for several decades. Since the earliest considerations of these systems, from the observations of dust in comet tails, the investigations of the planetary rings of the outer planets of the solar system, and the transport of dust on airless bodies such as the moon and meteors, there has been a basic understanding of the potential coupling between a background plasma and charged dust particles. With the first observations of dust formation in processing experiments and the start of dedicated laboratory studies of the properties of dusty plasmas starting in the early 1990’s, it became possible to perform detailed investigations of the interactions between the dust particles and the plasma. As the capabilities of laboratory studies have continued to mature, experimental devices such as the Magnetized Dusty Plasma Experiment (MDPX) at Auburn University [1] have been able to provide a flexible, multi-user research platform that can explore a wide variety of dusty plasma phenomena with and without magnetic fields that can be scaled to support research questions from fusion to space plasma investigations.

articleTitle: Resection Strategy for the Multi-level Plane Wave Time Domain Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents a resection strategy for the disaggregation in the multi-level plane wave time domain algorithm. The plane wave time domain algorithm is the counterpart to the frequency domain fast multipole methods and makes it possible to analyze the transient scattering from large and complex objects. By deriving the length of the relevant intervals to reconstruct the field in a given time interval, the resection strategy is described in detail. Finally, the validity of this resection approach is demonstrated by showing that the correct fields can be reconstructed exactly up to a controllable error.

articleTitle: Point-in-Domain Algorithm for Precise Near Field Calculations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Method of Moment (MoM) applied to Surface Integral Equations (SIEs) represents one of the most effective methods for full wave analysis of composite metallic and dielectric structures in the frequency domain. Recently, it was demonstrated that this method is also powerful tool for simulation of Medical MicroWave Imaging (MMWI) scenarios [1, 2]. Among others such simulations require highly accurate and efficient evaluation of the near field in the dense grid of points in human phantoms.

articleTitle: Supertoroidal Electrodynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Toroidal electrodynamics is a recently established research area of electromagnetism that involves the study of doughnut-shaped excitations in matter and in free-space. Despite being first considered over 60 years ago, toroidal excitations have been often omitted from the description of matter as they were considered negligible, high order corrections. Owing to the rapid recent advances in metamaterials, toroidal excitations were experimentally observed for the first time in arrays of toroidal metamolecules, providing dominant contributions to the metamaterial response and resulting in counter-intuitive phenomena, such as non-radiating configurations (anapoles) and vector potential sources. More recently, the field of toroidal electrodynamics expanded to include free-space propagating excitations in the form of toroidal light pulses. Such pulses, also known as Flying Doughnuts, are single cycle, space-time non-separable, broadband pulses of toroidal topology. They have been shown to preferentially excite toroidal and anapole resonant modes in nanoparticles and were generated only recently for the first time.

articleTitle: Comparison of Classic and Generalized Intersection Approach for the Synthesis of Transmitarrays with Near-field Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this work, two different methods based on the Intersection Approach (IA) for the synthesis of transmitarrays are compared. The first method leverages the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to efficiently seek solutions when constraints are enforced only on planes parallel to the radiating aperture. The second method aims to overcome the limitations of the first one in terms of generality, using a different model for the near-field computation and an alternative algorithm for the backward operator. To benchmark the two methods, the synthesis of a relatively large (576 elements) Ka-band transmitarray with a shaped near-field pattern is performed. The results reveal certain advantages and disadvantages for each method. The classic IA demonstrates faster convergence to a solution due the reduced computational complexity of the FFT. Conversely, the generalized IA yields slightly better fulfillment of the imposed requirements. Importantly, both solutions closely align with the challenging objectives of the synthesis.

articleTitle: The Platform for Earth Observation from Space in the framework of the Italian PNRR - Next Generation EU
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The “Monitoring Earth’s Evolution and Tectonics” (MEET) project is funded by the Italian “Piano Nazionale di Ripresa e Resilienza (PNRR) – Next Generation EU”, approved by the Ministry of University and Research. MEET is in the framework of the Research Infrastructure European Plate Observing System “EPOS” and aims to strengthen the observational systems dedicated to discovering the Earth’s dynamics, focusing on the Italian territory, particularly those regions more affected by natural hazards.

articleTitle: High Frequency Em Scattering by a Large Building With Multiple Windows
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In large cities where people congregate and live in high-rise buildings, the calculation and evaluation of the scattering field by a building with many windows is critical to ensuring the quality of wireless communication services. In this study, a closed-form solution for the far-field scattering by a building with conductive exterior walls and multiple windows has been developed based on the Kirchhoff Approximation (KA).

articleTitle: On some Operator Filtering Strategies Based on Suitably Modified Green’s Functions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Recent contributions showed the benefits of operator filtering for both preconditioning and fast solution strategies. While previous contributions leveraged laplacian-based filters, in this work we introduce and study a different approach leveraging the truncation of appropriately chosen spectral representations of operators’ kernels. In this contribution, the technique is applied to the operators of the 2D TE- and TM-electric field integral equations (EFIE). We explore two different spectral representations for the 2D Green’s function that lead to two distinct types of filtering of the EFIE operators. Numerical results corroborate the effectiveness of the newly proposed approaches, also in the Calderón preconditioned EFIE.

articleTitle: Beam modelling accuracy for flux calibration of phased array radio telescopes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The gain of radio telescopes is calibrated using well-known radio astronomical sources. Due to the limited number of suitable calibration sources, the angle between the directions towards the calibrator and towards the observed field can be as large as ~ 60°. This poses an instrument characterization and modelling challenge for phased array radio telescopes like LOFAR and SKA, which are steered electronically, as the gain of the antennas varies over the sky. We derive a requirement on the accuracy of the instrument model and assess the impact of two simplified calculations of the main beam peak gain of the subarrays (stations) of the low-frequency receiving system of the SKA. We show that station beam peak gain modelling can be simplified by using the average EEP, while the isolated antenna pattern is an oversimplification.

articleTitle: Research on the Coupling between High-voltage Cables and Low-voltage Cables in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: There are a lot of cables in electric vehicles, and cables layout is complex. The space inside an electric vehicle is small. Even if the high-voltage and low-voltage cables are not routed side by side, the electromagnetic emission from the high-voltage cables may affect the signals transmitted from the low-voltage cables in the same space. In this paper, the coupling between high and low voltage cables of a control device in an electric vehicle is studied, and the influence of different grounding conditions of high voltage cables on low voltage control signal cables is analyzed

articleTitle: Circular Array Synthesis for Cylindrical Beam-Scanning Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In the complex next-generation wireless communications scenario (i.e. 5G/6G and beyond), the radiating system should be designed to provide higher data rates, greater coverage, and improved reliability, while also meeting the constraints of size, cost, and environmental conditions. In this challenging framework, there is a growing interest in reconfigurable beam-shaping and beam-scanning antennas. However, traditional solutions based on phased arrays, although providing good radiation features, are characterized by a significant complexity and high cost. Hence, recently, new solutions based on reflective or transmitting metasurfaces have been proposed to create feasible, economical, agile and flexible beam-scanning and/or beam-shaping antennas [1]–[4].

articleTitle: Wideband Antenna Design for Time Domain RFI Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a wideband antenna that will be used for time domain RFI measurements in the SKA radio telescope project context. The time required for the RFI qualification of equipment used on a radio telescope site can be reduced by performing the qualification measurements in the time domain. A wideband antenna that can handle pulsed time domain signals is needed to allow this. The Vivaldi antenna is a frequency-independent antenna widely used in Ultra Wideband (UWB) applications and is here adapted for a lower frequency band. It is investigated in simulation for time-domain use by measuring the time signal transmitted by the antenna. Simulations of the design show that an impedance bandwidth from 57 MHz to beyond 6 GHz is achieved and that time domain pulses are transmitted and received with limited distortion, which is confirmed by an improved high fidelity factor compared to the LPDA currently in use for RFI qualification measurements.

articleTitle: Compact Wide-Scan Dual-Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna Array Based on LTCC Technology for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A compact dual-polarized (DP) dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) for two dimensional (2D) wide-angle scanning phased arrays operating at 28 GHz is presented. The proposed design is based on low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology by virtue of the benefits in terms of scalability at millimeter-wave (mmW) frequencies. The developed DRA element integrates two stacked cylindrical dielectric resonators (DRs) surrounded by a metal frame and is fed through a cross-shaped slot. An annular cavity separates the stacked DRs from the metal frame near the antenna aperture to enhance the active impedance-matching to air. The DRA element is analyzed in the infinite array environment and is characterized using an 8 × 8 array architecture consisting of 2 × 2 subarray tiles. This design is optimized for operation in the n261 band (27.5-28.35 GHz) with the active reflection coefficient |Γ| ≤ −10 dB across the targeted ±60° scan range. The array features a scan loss ranging from 3.2 dB to 3.9 dB in the H-, D-, and V-planes for both polarizations.

articleTitle: Stability of Transient Coupled Multi-Model Discrete Electromagnetic Field Formulations Using the Port-Hamiltonian System Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The port-Hamiltonian system (pHS) framework established for coupled system formulations in multi-model and multi-physics problems considers physical model formulations either in a continuous setting as sets of partial differential equations or, alternatively, in discrete variants as pH differential-algebraic equations (pH-DAEs) [1]. articleTitle: How Insights from EM Theory Have Guided Surgical Practice to Make MRI Safer for Patients with Active Electronic Implants
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has revolutionized our understanding of human biology and pathology, yet its accessibility remains limited to a growing group of patients with conductive implants. This has become an increasingly critical issue, as it is estimated that 75% of patients with implants will need at least one MRI exam during their lifetime [1] with many requiring repeated examinations, highlighting the pressing need to find a solution to this problem. The major risk of MRI in patients with active implantable medical devices (AIMDs) is the RF heating of the tissue, which can result in serious injuries. Despite extensive regulatory and technical efforts spanning two decades to enhance MR-conditional devices, a significant obstacle continues to hinder patient care: RF heating in MRI is significantly influenced by the implant’s configuration, leading to a broad range of heating variation observed in patients with the same implant, up to two orders of magnitude. Here we show that simple EM-guided modifications in routing of AIMD leads can significantly reduce MRI-induced RF heating in patients with deep brain stimulation (DBS) devices and cardiac implantable medical devices (CIEDs).

articleTitle: A low-cost wide-angle coverage rectennas for energy harvesting applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We present a compact, effective, and broad-angle array of rectennas designed for harvesting energy and transmitting wireless power in the mid-band of 6G. Specifically, the device comprises a group of on-board Bruce-array antennas that operate at the same frequency (12 GHz) but have varying radiation angles. This configuration enables spatial multiplexing for efficient harvesting of radiative energy. The Bruce-array antennas are capable to receive RF signals with incidence angles spanning from -60° to 60°, offering a peak gain exceeding 7.89 dBi. Additionally, a suitable power management system is proposed for this arrayed rectenna system. The rectenna panel achieves a conversion efficiency of 60% when subjected to an input power of -2.2 dBm across a wide reception range.

articleTitle: Method of characteristics applied to stochastic Maxwell’s equations in the chaos basis expansion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Wiener polynomial chaos basis has been used to develop stochastic partial (and ordinary) differential equations (PDE, ODE) suitable for analyzing uncertainty quantification (UQ) [1]. A virtue of the approach is that one can quantify the statistical behavior of the output with a few terms rather than thousands of Monte Carlo (MC) runs using the original equations. This method has been applied to an FDTD implementation of hydro-acoustics [2]. We consider a representation of Maxwell’s time dependent equations for the fields $\vec{D}$ and $\vec{B}$, in terms of the material parameters $M=\varepsilon^{-1}$ and $R=\mu^{-1}$. Expanding these fields and parameters in a polynomial chaos basis $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}F^{(k)}\Phi^{(k)}(\theta)$, etc., where $\Phi^{(k)}(\theta)$ is the basis set and $F^{(k)}$ is a set of weights $(F$ represents any of the fields in the problem) leads to equation (1), where $\delta_{ikj}=\int\Phi^{(i)}\Phi^{(k)}\Phi^{(j)}d\theta$.

articleTitle: Antenna Position Estimation Results from In-Situ Measurement Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, legacy data from an in-situ measurement campaign that was performed on a compact sub-array of Low Band Antennas (LBAs) of the LOFAR radio telescopes are used to illustrate the effectiveness of a recently developed antenna element position estimation method. The method allows recovery from aliasing after sub-sampling of odd harmonic signals transmitted from an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) with a known position in the sky. This allows not just small errors due to element placement deviations from the designed positions to be detected, but also large errors due to the incorrect connection of antenna elements to the digital back-end, or malfunction of receiver amplifiers. The results look promising and can be improved by using an increased number of samples from a suitable UAV flight path, and by updating the data model to include calculation of the phase errors from the analog receiver signal paths.

articleTitle: Hyperthermia Treatment Planning Using Shape Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The goal of hyperthermia treatment planning is to selectively elevate the temperature of cancerous tissue to around $42^{\circ}C$ while avoiding damage to healthy tissue. This is achieved using exterior exciting coils surrounding the affected body part, such as the thigh. However, optimizing the shape and location of these coils presents a two-part challenge. The first step involves solving for the electric field, which determines the Joule heating in different parts of the body. The second step involves determining the resulting temperature distribution, which is dependent on the material properties that change with temperature. To address this inverse optimization problem, this paper proposes the use of the genetic algorithm (GA). By adjusting the shape of the conductor as the temperature changes, the optimal coil distribution is obtained to achieve the desired temperature distribution in a human thigh.

Author Keywords: finite elements methods for coupled problems

articleTitle: Composite Vortex Theory as a New Design Strategy for Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) or, more in general, Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) are promising technologies that could revolutionize wireless communication systems, by enhancing signal strength, coverage, and security, as well as by reducing interference and energy consumption [1]–[4]. Indeed, the interaction of the electromagnetic waves with the propagating environment can be finely controlled by covering environmental objects with planar structures, whose electromagnetic response can be engineered and, eventually, electronically adjusted for achieving anomalous reflection/transmission properties.

articleTitle: Comparison of TE11- and TE01-Mode Excitation in Overmoded Waveguides for Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Radar-based sensors are widely used in industrial applications. Apart from standard distance measurements, further radar-based analytical measurements came into focus in recent years. Typically, the radar excites the fundamental TE10- or TE11-mode using rectangular waveguides or circular waveguides, respectively.

articleTitle: Narrowband Stimulated Radiation During Ionospheric Heating Experiments: Recent Observations, Theory, and Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Ground-based transmission of high-power high frequency (HF) radio waves into the Earth’s ionosphere produces a plethora of physical phenomena resulting from complex nonlinear processes. This field has commonly been referred to as ionospheric heating or ionospheric modification in pertinent literature, and it has a long, rich history dating back at least to the 1960s. Phenomena induced by the interaction of radio waves and the ionospheric plasma may serve as a laboratory for investigating fundamental electromagnetic wave phenomena as well as facilitate diagnostics for the near-earth space environment aeronomy. Although important phenomena produced during ionospheric heating include production of geo-magnetic field aligned density irregularities, optical emissions, and production of plasma turbulence, this presentation will primarily concentrate on a specific phenomenon which is stimulated secondary radiation that exists in the frequency band typically within roughly 1kHz of the transmit frequency ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>.
