articleTitle: A new metamaterial for MRI-safe deep brain stimulation leads
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) leads have become a valuable tool in neuroscience for diagnosing and treating various neurological conditions, including Parkinson’s disease [1]. However, commercially available leads have limited compatibility with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), hindering the possibility for patients with intracranial implants to benefit from the diagnostic potential of functional MRI [2]. Therefore, the development of MRI-safe DBS leads is necessary to promote new advances in the field. Here, we propose a novel technology to fabricate the internal microwires of DBS leads, that was specifically designed to ensure safe operation with MRI up to 3T. The technology is designed to include a steep interface between two segments of metals that are layered onto a non-conductive substrate. The abrupt resistance variation at the interface breaks up the RF-induced current, reducing distal electrode heating, specific absorption rate (SAR), and MRI artifacts [3].

articleTitle: Analysis of Heating Characteristics of Rectangular Resonant Cavity Applicator for Deep Heating of Abdominal Tumors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In recent years, hyperthermia, which is considered a minimally invasive treatment method, has attracted attention. Hyperthermia is a treatment based on the clinical fact that cancerous tissues are less tolerant to heat than normal tissues. Heating cancerous tissue to approximately 42°C for a period of time kills only the cancerous tissue while normal tissue survives. In our previous study, a cylindrical cavity resonator was proposed for hyperthermia treatment of abdominal tumors. However, the proposed applicator required a large area of the human body to be placed inside the applicator, and there was a possibility that unintended parts of the body might be heated. Therefore, in this study, the shape of the applicator was changed from cylindrical to rectangular and redesigned to minimize the area of the human body to be placed inside the applicator. In this study, the heating characteristics of the proposed rectangular applicator were numerically investigated by performing an electromagnetic field analysis using two different resonance patterns.

articleTitle: Characterization of the Beam and the Aperture of the Onsala Twin Telescopes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) was originally developed to perform high angular resolution radio imaging, but it has also proven useful in geodesy. VLBI has played a key role in defining the International Celestial Reference Frame (ICRF), providing measurements of the Earth Orientation Parameters (EOP), and contributing to the International Terrestrial Reference Frame (ITRF) [1]. The legacy S/X VLBI systems have achieved positional accuracies of up to 5 mm.

articleTitle: Modal Amplitudes of Electromagnetic Fields in a Conical Cavity: A Novel Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The aim of this study is to add to the current advancements in the study of microwave resonant cavities by presenting an analytical solution in the time domain for electromagnetic fields in regular conical lines that share a common apex. The solution is derived by employing the evolutionary approach to electrodynamics (EAE) and incorporating the newly proposed format of Maxwell’s equations in SI units.

articleTitle: Design of a Multi-layer Dual-band Frequency Selective Surface Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A multi-layer cascaded passive bandpass frequency selective surface is presented in this paper. It provides a narrow and wideband passband in the frequency range of 2 to 8 GHz. It is based on a square patch and aperture with a double split ring-shaped slot in the middle layers. The FSS demonstrates bandpass response of higher order with three transmission poles at 4.5-6 GHz band and one pole at 4.2 GHz. The passbands are significantly distanced by two transmission zeros at 4.4 GHz and 4.6 GHz, resulting in substantial out-of-band rejection. It is illustrated that changing the split ring slot’s gap can control thepoles, then one design is selected as optimum.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of RCS Reduction by Metasurfaces Based on Scattering Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper reports a method for bandwidth enhancement of radar cross section (RCS) reduction by metasurfaces. Scattering cancellation is one of the common methods for reducing RCS of target scatterers. It occurs when the wave reflected by the target scatterer and the wave reflected by the cancelling scatterer are the same amplitude and opposite phase. Since the bandwidth of the scattering cancellation is usually narrow, we propose a bandwidth enhancement method by metasurfaces that can control the frequency dependence of the scattering phase. We designed and fabricated a metasurface composed of a patch array on a grounded dielectric substrate. We confirmed that the metasurface gives broader bandwidth of 10dB RCS reduction than the metallic canceling scatterer.

articleTitle: Discontinuous Galerkin Formulation for Modelling Multiple Material and Multiple Conductor Junctions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Discontinuous Galerkin (DG) [1–3] implementations applied to surface integral equation (SIE) method of moments (MoM) [4] formulations (and expedited via multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) [5] and domain decomposition method (DDM) [6]), have brought the possibility of solving complex electromagnetic (EM) scattering problems through the use of nonconformal meshes. Such possibility is very appealing, especially in the context of DDM, as it allows the different subdomains to be modeled and meshed independently, without paying attention to the concordance of mesh in the tear contours between them. This greatly simplifies the CAD generation and meshing processes.

articleTitle: Volcanic plumes detection and retrievals from remote sensing systems: recent development and future improvements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Explosive eruptions produce high amount of volcanic particles (tephra) and gases (mainly H2O, CO2 and SO2) that are dispersed in the atmosphere forming volcanic clouds. Tephra particles have highly variable sizes (from microns to decimetres), very irregular shapes and variable compositions. The dispersal and the fallout of tephra are one of the most important volcanic causes of health problems, damage of critical infrastructures and aviation disruptions. In order to mitigate the effects of volcanic plumes on environment and society, a reliable discrimination and retrievals of volcanic plumes characteristics are needed. During the last years, remote sensing techniques have increased their capability to analyse the volcanic activity. The development of new sensors and the improvement of new algorithms, many of them satellite-based (Corradini et al., 2018), have in fact increased our capability to give reliable assessments in near real time (Scollo et al., 2019). Different sensors, spanning from microwave (MW) to thermal infrared (TIR) wavelengths, are sometimes integrated to capture the wide range of class-sizes within the volcanic plumes. In this work we show how TIR radiometric data, in some cases used in conjunction with MW and millimetre-wave (MMW) measurements, can give a complete characterization of volcanic plumes. Here we will show some applications to the Calbuco (Chile) 2015 eruption and the recent Etna (Italy) explosive activity, characterized by more than 60 powerful lava fountains in less than 2 years (Figure 1, left). To assure reliable and accurate results, a products validation is needed. Here, the results obtained for Etna are compared with data coming from several ground-based instruments installed around the volcano (Figure 1, right).

articleTitle: Hybrid Cartesian/unstructured numerical method for efficient resolution of Maxwell’s equations in time domain: Application to buried object detection from airborne remote sensing platforms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The growing concern in the study of system electromagnetic environment is frequently dealt with simulation tools. Due to the increasing complexity of structures, more and more efficient simulation methods are required. Currently, the most widely used basic method for solving unsteady Maxwell’s equations is the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique based on Yee’s scheme [1] which is computationally very efficient. This is partly due to the fact that it is based on a Cartesian mesh requiring little storage and few operations at each time iteration. However, this requirement for Cartesian meshes brings difficulties when dealing with curved geometries and leads to an inaccuracy in field computation in their vicinities. Other methods, such as finite-volume time-domain (FVTD) techniques, have thus been studied using unstructured meshes composed of tetrahedral cells [2]. The disadvantage of these methods is their rather high computational and memory cost compared to Yee’s approach. A natural idea is then to use a hybrid Cartesian/unstructured mesh with a limited area of tetrahedral cells around the object. Previous studies have proposed different hybridization methods between FVTD and FDTD schemes but without necessarily ensuring stability [3].

articleTitle: Advanced Error Estimation, Adaptive Refinement, and Uncertainty Quantification Methodologies in Frequency-Domain Computational Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Error estimation and control, adaptive refinement, and uncertainty quantification are essential for modern effective and reliable simulation-based design in mission-critical electromagnetic applications ranging from antennas and propagation to electromagnetic compatibility and microelectronics. This paper presents recent advances in accelerated, rigorous, adaptive, goal-oriented error estimation and control, model refinement, and uncertainty quantification for frequency-domain computational electromagnetics (CEM).

articleTitle: A non-Overlapping Time Domain Decomposition Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Nowadays, electromagnetic performance analysis is an integral part of electric and electronic systems development and must be considered during the design phase of the studied systems. Numerous electromagnetic numerical tools exist to solve these systems. However, the complexity of the phenomena to be solved translated by the multitude of scales and numerical methods remains an issue. On the other hand, domain decomposition (DD) methods allow solving a complex problem by breaking it into simpler sub-problems [1]. Generally, the most suitable numerical method is applied to each sub-domain. The global solution is retrieved based on the partial solution of each sub-model through interface conditions. However, most existing methods are in the frequency domain with overlapping interfaces. In the time domain, methods such as temporal hybridization are synchronous and share numerical models [2]. In this work, we rely on [3] to use a temporal domain decomposition method allowing fully asynchronous simulations of the sub-systems while preserving the confidentiality of the numerical models.

articleTitle: Reflective metasurface for simultaneous generation of Fronthaul and Backhaul Linken mm-Wave FR2 communications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The utilization of mm-Wave spectrum is gaining interest with the advent of the 5G and upcoming generations like 6G, aiming to provide high-speed wireless access in cellular networks. These systems are anticipated to operate in frequency bands from 20 to 300 GHz, increasing the capacity of the system and reducing the latency compared to their predecessors. The use of mm-Wave spectrum in communication poses novel challenges concerning signal propagation characteristics [1]. Higher frequencies result in faster signal attenuation (increased path loss) and greater susceptibility to physical barriers, as the penetration losses become more prominent. In outdoor scenarios such as streets, the coverage provided by a base station (BS) may be disrupted by densely populated areas with numerous buildings, whereas indoor scenarios (shopping malls, airports and so on) may experience coverage limitations due to obstructions like walls or furniture. Consequently, these factors give rise to areas with inadequate or nonexistent coverage, commonly known as blind zones. A low-complex and cost-effective solution involves deploying femtocell BS that are specifically adapted to the blind zone. In this scenario, the BS would generate a fronthaul (FH) link that covers the blind zone. However, the BS still requires a high-capacity backhaul (BH) link, typically implemented through wired solutions (i.e., optic fiber). As a result, this deployment can become expensive due to the need for costly BH infrastructure. In this line, a common approach is using Reflective Intelligent Surfaces (RIS). However, existing RIS implementations primarily focus on tilting the FH link, especially the RIS-1 and RIS-2 [2].

articleTitle: Circuit design with energy storage circuit that operates on low power for WIPT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In recent years, sensors have been installed every-where in our daily lives to monitor human flow due to COVID-19 pandemic and for inventory control in warehouses.It is impractical to supply power and information to these IoT devices and sensors individually, and the use of microwave-based WIPT (Wireless Information and Power Transmission) for data and power transmission to each sensor is being considered. However, long-distance transmission is difficult due to the large free-space loss in the current microwave-based WIPT.In this research, we investigate a system and a device of a repeater to improve the transmission efficiency and extend the transmission distance of the WIPT system. In this paper, we report on the design and fabrication of a circuit for storing reliable power at low input power.

articleTitle: Highly Selective Third-Order Bandpass Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Frequency selective surface (FSS) is a kind of spatial filter, which is used in wide applications such as radomes, polarizers, and filters due to its capability of controlling electromagnetic waves [1]. Traditional FSSs consist of a two-dimensional periodic array of unit cells, however, such a single-layer surface often suffers from poor filtering characteristics. Furthermore, designing FSSs with a higher-order bandpass response to achieve a wider transmission band has also attracted intensive investigations [2].

articleTitle: Extended Physical Optics Approximation For Edge Diffraction By Dielectric Wedges
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this investigation, an extension of the physical optics (PO) approximation method has been applied to evaluate the edge diffraction of the electromagnetic wave by two-dimensional dielectric wedges. Uniform asymptotic solutions have been obtained for the TM and TE polarizations. The PO formulation for a conducting wedge [1] has been extended to treat a dielectric wedge. Equivalent electric and magnetic currents on the wedge surface are determined from the geometrical optic (GO) fields.

articleTitle: A Study on Fast Inverse Laplace Transform for Transient Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Signals with wide frequency band are often used in recent applications of electromagnetic waves and, therefore, the time-domain simulations are becoming more important. The most successful of these may be the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method [1] and it is used in a wide variety of transient phenomena. Basic idea of the FDTD method is simple but its computational cost sometimes limits the scope of application. On the other hand, the frequency-domain approaches have a long history, and we have a vast store of knowledge. In this study, the fast inverse Laplace transform (FILT) [2] is investigated to apply the frequency-domain techniques to the transient analyses.

articleTitle: Single Source Formulation for the Scattering/Transmission Problem by Penetrable Targets including Conducting Multi-Screens
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The design of many moderns devices contains conducting multi-screens, i.e. metallic constructs made up from three or more surfaces that meet at so-called junctions. Notable examples are via-holes in high frequency printed circuit boards and integrated chips.

articleTitle: Numerical Investigation of Heating Characteristics Depending on Ultrasound Irradiation Position During HIFU Treatment.
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: High Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU) is a minimally invasive treatment that focuses ultrasound waves emitted from a transducer into the interior of cancerous tissue and ablates the tissue with the thermal energy generated at the focal point. Generally, ultrasound waves are reflected when they hit high-density materials such as bone, and there is a risk of damaging normal tissue. Therefore, it has been difficult to treat areas surrounded by bone with HIFU. In this study, the reflection of ultrasound from bone surfaces during HIFU treatment was analyzed by computer simulation using an anatomical human model.

articleTitle: Method of integral summation identities in the problem of a TE-polarized electromagnetic wave diffraction on a vertical barrier in an infinite waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper the boundary value problem (BVP) for the Helmholtz equation associated with the diffraction of a TE-polarized electromagnetic wave on a vertical barrier in an infinite waveguide is investigated. Using the partial domain method the BVP is reduced to an infinite system of linear algebraic equations of the second kind (ISLAE-2). The equivalence of the initial BVP and the ISLAE-2 and the Fredholm property of the matrix operator of ISLAE-2 in the weighted Hilbert space of infinite sequences that ensures the fulfillment of energy (edge) condition are proved. The truncation (reduction) method is developed on the basis of semi-regularization for the approximate solution of ISLAE-2. Broad series of computational experiments are performed.

Author Keywords: infinite system of linear algebraic equations

articleTitle: Optimization Process for Bending a Periodic Structure: Start Ahead with Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: optimizing high-dimensional designs requires essential efforts; bending of a radiating device is one of such examples. Such appearance appears in various applications like medical, space, radar, etc. Consequently, strong numerical methods are becoming necessary. In the present work, an optimized bent periodic structure, multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) antenna designed through a neural network (NN) is presented. The main goal of this optimization is to focus on the curvature of the antenna to find the suitable results for S-parameters both in terms of reflection S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, and transmission S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> coefficients, and also total active reflection coefficient (TARC). Through the proposed method, the antenna configuration loaded by meandered slot and surrounded by printed meander line of different periodicities is designed and optimized in three frequency bands within the 12.94 GHz to 25 GHz range, namely, 12.94 - 14.79 GHz, 16.09 - 17.25 GHz, and 19.17 - 25 GHz.

articleTitle: Study Regarding the Influence of the Biasing Network in Designing a Switchable Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper some hints on the design of a switchable Frequency Selective Surface are proposed. The simulations of two distinct metallic constructions are performed, initially with no control network present and afterwards with control network (having the function to bias the active components inside the unit cells). The suggested designs have been evaluated using electromagnetic simulation. Different filtering bands are obtained below 12 GHz using the periodicity of the square-shaped unit cell with an 18 mm edge length.

articleTitle: Systematic Self-Interference Mitigation In Full Duplex Antenna Arrays Via Transmit Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The optimal antenna array excitation vector is derived that maximizes the (realized) array gain in a particular direction while preventing the coupled input power to the low-noise amplifiers on the receive side to exceed a certain maximum threshold level. This is very useful for in-band full-duplex systems where the hardware complexity for self-interference cancellation must be minimized. In this approach, the perfect nulling of interference on the RX side is not required, sparing degrees of freedom for the TX beamformer. We evaluate the performance of the proposed TX beamforming algorithm by showing numerical results of the 25 x-polarized TX and 25 RX with 0.5$\lambda$ element spacing and $\lambda$ gap distance between the TX and RX sub-array.

articleTitle: Extension of the Higher-Order Array Decomposition Method for Arrays with Non-identical Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Higher-Order Array Decomposition Method (HO-ADM) is extended to arrays with non-identical elements. This extension is achieved by appropriate manipulation of the FFT-accelerated matrix-vector product (MVP), special meshing, and by hiding a selected subset of unknowns in the iterative solution process. We demonstrate that the simulation time for a 1024-element patch array can be reduced by an order of magnitude by employing HO-ADM compared to other fast methods such as MLFMM.

articleTitle: Wiener-Hopf Solution of Diffraction by a PEC Wedge in Anisotropic Media
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this work we present our recent work on novel Wiener-Hopf(WH) formulation for the analysis and the study of scattering of wedges [1] immersed in complex materials [2–3]. We start from an original study of the perfect electrically conducting (PEC) wedge immersed in uniaxial ($\varepsilon_{\mathrm{x}}$=$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{y}}\boldsymbol{\neq}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{z}},\ \mathrm{\mu}_{\mathrm{x}}$=$\mathrm{\mu}_{\mathrm{y}}\boldsymbol{\neq}\mathrm{\mu}_{\mathrm{z}}$) and biaxial (all different $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{i}}, \mathrm{\mu}_{\mathrm{i}}$=x,y,z) media illuminated by plane waves, where the wedge has an aperture angle of 2$\pi$-2$\gamma$. The uniaxial case has been studied by Felsen in [4], however generalization and exploitation of this case has not been further carried out in literature.

articleTitle: Advanced modeling techniques for accurate and efficient particle-in-cell simulations of laser-plasma accelerators
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In a laser-plasma accelerator, an intense laser pulse drives a plasma wave that can trap and accelerate electrons to GeV energies over few centimeter distances. This relatively new accelerator technology promises compact sources of high-brightness beams that would benefit a variety of applications in science, medicine and industry.

articleTitle: Low Profile 3-D Printed Transmitarray for Future 6G Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A preliminary investigation of the possibility to exploit three-dimensional (3D) printing technology for the fabrication of a transmitarray (TA) is addressed. More in detail, both dielectric and metallic unit cells are designed with the purpose of providing a non-uniform phase profile of the TA panel to collimate the main beam at broadside direction ($\theta$=0°).

articleTitle: Modified multipoles in metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Multipole decomposition method is a promising tool for investigation of radiating or scattering response of electromagnetic sources or particles. It works even in the case of relatively complicated and compound scatterers like multilayer particles, clusters, asymmetrical systems, and metamaterials [1]. Commonly, the radiation fields of point electric or magnetic sources are decomposed only into electric or magnetic dipole moments, while real sources can be described by series of multipoles, including higher multipoles and toroidal moments. For instance, toroidal or anapole metamaterials cannot be correctly described without taking into consideration toroidal multipoles [2].

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of the Bit Error Induced by EMI on Galvanically Isolated Data-Link Embedded in an Automotive Battery Management IC
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, the susceptibility to electromagnetic interference (EMI) of a battery management system (BMS) used in electric vehicles is addressed. In particular, the effects of EMI on the BMS vertical interface (VIF), i.e., the galvanically isolated data link between different BMS modules are analyzed by transistor-level simulations with reference to direct power injection (DPI) and bulk current injection (BCI) test conditions for the first time. Based on the simulations, the DPI and BCI susceptibility levels of two different VIF architectures are estimated, and different failure mechanisms are highlighted.

articleTitle: Signals of Opportunity Reflectometry at Multiple Frequencies and Polarizations: Simulation Studies and Instrument Validation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Signals of Opportunity reflectometry (SoOp-R) employs existing non-cooperative transmitters as sources of illumination in bistatic radar. In the typical application, these sources are communication satellites. Cross-correlation between a direct line of sight signal and a reflected path signal (or autocorrelation of the combined signal) can be used as an observation to estimate the surface complex reflection coefficient. SoOp-R enables microwave remote sensing observations to be made in bands allocated for communications and is thus not limited to frequencies protected for science use. P-band (<500 MHz) is of particular value as those frequencies are heavily used for communications and have no protected bands. Only P-band is capable of penetrating below the top few cm of the soil, to provide sensitivity to the root-zone soil moisture (RZSM). Presently no direct retrievals of RZSM are available from spaceborne instruments (although there are some data assimilation products using surface soil moisture from L-band observations).

articleTitle: On the Evaluation of Retarded-Time Potentials due to CRWG Functions: Self-Term Case
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A scheme to evaluate the retarded-time potentials due to curvilinear Rao-Wilton-Glisson (CRWG) functions is presented for the self-term case, i.e., when the observation point is in the source triangle. Using the Radon transform interpretation of the radiation integrals, the surface integral is reduced to a line integral on the intersection of the sphere centered to the observation point and the support of the CRWG function, i.e., high order triangles. The line integral is evaluated using the suitable order Gauss-Legendre quadrature rule (GLQR). It is shown that the kernel of the resulting line integral does not exhibit any singular behavior as time tends to zero. A numerical example is presented to demonstrate the accuracy and validity of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Deployment Errors for A Two-Stage Antenna in CubeSat Constellations at THz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The rise of CubeSats in non-terrestrial networks (NTN) has gained recent popularity. To make such CubeSat constellations work at faster rates, the utilization of the terahertz (THz) band is proposed. As such, both high gain directional communications as well as expedited neighbor discovery should be possible, to which end a two Stage antenna is proposed, and analyzed. Stage 1 is set in-vitro within the CubeSat, while Stage 2 is deployed later via a crank-shaft-based hinge mechanism. Possible errors in deployment are analyzed, including both symmetrical and asymmetrical errors. It is shown that while symmetrical errors can completely cripple the additional gain from Stage 2, asymmetrical errors can still result in an antenna design that provides 5 dBi of additional gain without any real estate penalty.

articleTitle: P.T.D and Rotational Symmetries in Non-Reflecting Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: $\mathcal{P}\cdot\mathcal{T}\cdot\mathcal{D}$ and rotational symmetries of electromagnetic and photonic systems have recently been shown, separately, to characterize different non-reflecting structures. In this work, we provide a general framework for both types of symmetries, casting the rotational symmetry in terms of a new $\mathcal{R}\cdot\mathcal{T}\cdot\mathcal{D}$ - type symmetry. Out of this analysis, a third option emerges; namely, a combined $\mathcal{P}\cdot\mathcal{T}\cdot\mathcal{D}/\mathcal{R}\cdot\mathcal{T}\cdot\mathcal{D}$ symmetry condition. With this option, the door opens for synthesis of many new non-reflecting media, as shown in the examples below.

articleTitle: Start Vector Estimation for Iterative Multiple-Frequency Inverse Source Solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The iterative solution of inverse source problems for multiple frequencies can be accelerated by start vector estimates obtained from already available solutions. Such methods working with certain kinds of projections have been in particular around for the solution of linear systems of equations with multiple excitations but identical system matrix. For multiple frequency inverse source solutions, such methods are shown to work very well with a very interesting solution behavior.

articleTitle: Transionospheric Autofocus for Synthetic Aperture Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) illuminates the target with microwaves and uses digital signal processing to build the image. For a spaceborne SAR, the antenna is mounted on a satellite, whereas the target area is on the ground. The antenna emits pulses of electromagnetic radiation and receives the returns, i.e., signals reflected off the target. The signal processing algorithm takes into account multiple pulses emitted and received by the antenna at a series of its successive positions, called the synthetic aperture. The resulting image approximates the backscattering reflectivity of the target. Mathematically, SAR imaging is equivalent to solving an inverse problem - that of reconstructing the unknown target reflectivity given radar returns as the input data.

articleTitle: Suppression of Scattering for Small Dielectric Particles: Anapole Mode and Invisibility
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In 1962, Peter Uiimtsev proposed the idea of implementing invisibility using a special geometric shape of the body that minimizes backscattering [1]. Such a configuration can be realized, for example, with a conical mirror directed towards the light source. The practical implementation of this idea led to the creation of stealth technology. Another idea was proposed in 1983 by M. Kerker. It is based on the use of optical materials with ε = μ [2]. The next step was the idea of an optical transformation based on Fermat’s principle. Inhomogeneous media with special profiles of dielectric and magnetic permeability (ε = ε (r) and μ = μ (r)) make it possible to “direct” light around the masking area [3, 4]. In the literature, the ideas of scattering suppression were also considered, based on multilayer metamaterials in the form of plasmonic and dielectric coatings [5, 6], as well as special dielectric structures realizing anapole states [7, 8] and bound states in a continuum [9]. It is possible to study the problem of scattering suppression by selecting a special radiation polarization, in which the scattered field lies in the region of invisible modes [10]. The second part of this problem is devoted to investigating the minimization of scattering by varying the shape and refractive index of the particle, which ensure the suppression of scattering in the case of a plane electromagnetic wave falling on the particle. An analytical study of scattering minimization is supposed to be carried out by the method of the so-called extended boundary conditions (the T-matrix method) [11] and the surface perturbation method [12], using the theory of perturbation of the particle surface with respect to a spherical one.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Millimeter Vortex Far-fields using Time-domain Surface Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In the last several decades, the optical vortex has been considered to be applied mainly to large capacity optical fiber communication [1] and an optical tweezer [2] based on its proper characteristics such as transport of orbital angular momentum and independent modes of spiral wave-front structures. Recently applications of the optical vortex phenomena are spreading out to other frequency ranges such as UV, X-ray, gamma-ray, millimeter and microwave. In particular, the millimeter wave vortex has been attracting many attentions in plasma science owing to possibility of strong interaction with plasmas. For example, it was pointed out that the millimeter wave vortex can propagate in weakly magnetized plasma, in which standard plane wave with the same frequency is in cut-off condition [3]. On the other hand, there still exist an important task to be solved for generation of stable propagation of the millimeter wave vortex. For example, it was pointed out that the hybrid mode HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mn</inf> carries well-defined orbital angular momentum and stably propagate in a corrugated circular waveguide [4]. However, generation method of such the stable millimeter wave vortex in free space is not found yet. In general, beam size of the optical vortex is about 100 time larger than that of optical wavelength. Accordingly it is not good way to generate the millimeter wave vortex by using the similar scheme as the optical vortex such as the Laguerre-Gaussian mode, otherwise size of the millimeter wave vortex beam reaches to several meters. Therefore, we need to carefully consider the generation method of much smaller size millimeter wave vortex, and then it is required to employ any full wave numerical field simulations. For example, beam size of the millimeter wave vortex propagating in the corrugated waveguide has at least 20 times larger than its wavelength [4]. This mean that the full wave simulation become extremely large scale computation and evaluation of far distance propagation of the millimeter wave vortex is almost impossible. In this work, we here consider to create the free space millimeter wave vortex by using the corrugated waveguide (Fig.1). Then the FDTD method is used for simulations of generation of the vortex fields at the corrugated waveguide and time-domain surface integral equation [5] is employed for evaluation of behavior of the vortex field at far distance (Fig.1).

articleTitle: Multimodal Wearable Sensing Systems based on Higher-Order Parity-Time Symmetry
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Parity-time (PT) symmetry, a salient landmark in the realm of non-Hermitian physics, reveals that non-conservative Hamiltonians upholding both parity (P) and time-reversal (T) operators may present entirely real eigenspectra [1]–[3]. The advent of PT symmetry has facilitated a plethora of applications, ranging from wireless sensor telemetry and power transmission to dynamic wave manipulation and cloaking [1], [2]. In particular, PT-symmetric systems have exhibited formidable efficacy in ultra-sensitive wireless sensing [3]. It has been observed that the eigen frequencies of such a system bifurcate at an exceptional point (EP), where they demonstrate remarkable sensitivity to minuscule perturbations. This phenomenon culminates in superlative sensitivity, considerably outstripping that of traditional $LC$ resonator-based sensors. Nonetheless, despite these appreciable benefits, current $PT -$symmetric systems are limited to the detection of singular resistive or capacitive parameters. These systems fall short in identifying and discerning each parameter when resistive and capacitive variations coexist. This constraint curtails the applicability of $PT -$symmetric systems in certain real-world scenarios. For instance, in wearable biomedical monitoring situations, multiple biomarkers may vary simultaneously, thereby necessitating more multiplexed detection systems.

articleTitle: Lower Hybrid Waves in the Auroral Ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The aurora is a microcosm of astrophysical plasmas where intense electron and ion beams are responsible for the generation of strong wave activity including powerful radio frequency emission known as Auroral kilometric radiation (AKR). In the aurora, turbulent wave fields close to the lower-hybrid fiequency exist, giving rise to one of the most important processes in turbulent plasmas — namely wave collapse and caviton formation. The special role lower-hybrid waves play in space physics is connected with the fact that these waves can be in simultaneous phase resonance with both electrons and ions transferring energy from one plasma component to another. A number of processes have been considered for the generation of this turbulent wave activity including electron beams and ion horseshoe distributions. The precipitating electrons responsible for the aurora can easily excite these wave modes and ion horseshoe distributions are another free energy source for the wave activity which is the most intense observed in the region. The lower-hybrid wave amplitude in the auroral zone is large enough to initiate modulational type interactions through the ponderomotive force exerted by the waves on the plasma particles and responsible for the creation of density cavitons through the evolution of strong turbulence. This is an important topic in plasma physics combining nonlinearity with complexity and exists in many types of plasma from laser fusion, tokomaks, space plasmas and astrophysical plasmas such as gamma ray bursts, relativistic jets and pulsars. The aurora therefore provides a unique and accessible environment to study strong turbulence effects. In this talk I will describe the modulational instability and wave collapse of lower-hybrid waves and the role they play in energizing particles.

articleTitle: Selective Laser Sintering of Waveguide Devices for 5G and 6G Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This article presents an overview of different waveguide devices implemented by additive manufacturing using the Selective Laser Sintering technique showing high performances for both terrestrial and space applications. Firstly, two types of mode two converters will be exposed. These broadband devices without resonant behaviour and without high electromagnetic field densities are especially well-suited to cope with the two main problems of additive manufacturing, i.e., the accuracy and the surface roughness. The first one is a T$E_{10}$ rectangular waveguide mode to T$E_{01}$ circular waveguide mode flared-type converter in Q-band and the second one is a T$E_{10}$ rectangular waveguide mode to T$M_{01}$ circular waveguide mode converter in Ku-band. Secondly, a compact ortho-mode transducer in Ku-band is presented with tested results similar to those obtained by milling or spark erosion suited for satellite applications. In all cases the experimental results of the prototypes are discussed in detail. In addition, the issues related to the orientation of the parts inside the building chamber and other undesirable effects such as spikes due to manufacturing asymmetries, are shared with the scientific community in other to contribute to the development of the additive manufacturing in microwave engineering.

articleTitle: Generation of a tunable Dual-frequency source by operating a laser at Period-one
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A novel method for the generation of a tunable dual-frequency laser source is presented. The proposed system uses a laser diode with optical feedback and operating at period-one (P1) oscillation state. Through investigation on the optical spectra of the laser at this state, dual-frequency components can be obtained and the separation (i.e., the difference) of the two frequencies can be flexibly adjusted from 2.72GHz to 3.12GHz by varying the external cavity length. Such dual-frequency feature and its tunable range have many potential applications for both optical and microwave measurement. The paper also presents an example of application by the proposed system, where a dual-frequency laser Doppler velocimeter (DV) is implemented for high-resolution target detection.

articleTitle: Threat Analysis of Vehicle Engine Electronic Control Unit in Severe Electromagnetic Pulse Environment and Research on Protection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The severe electromagnetic pulses generated by nuclear blast or high power microwave cause serious electromagnetic threats to the vehicle Electronic Control Unit (ECU) through the way of field-wire coupling. This kind of threat affects the performance of mobility, and also the vehicle safety. This paper focuses on a typical multi-use vehicle, the effect mechanism of the ECU in the severe electromagnetic environment is analyzed, the broadband Electro-Magnetic Pulse (EMP) radiated test for the vehicle is carried out, and the relationship between the operating state of the vehicle engine system and the coupled transient voltage on the power line of the ECU is analyzed. The test results show that the broadband EMP causes interference on the ECU through the power cable, and the overloaded coupling voltage resulting in the engine stalling. According to the analysis results, the multi-level protection circuit is designed for the power supply of the ECU. The electromagnetic protection is realized by cutting off the energy transmission path of the EMP threat, and the effectiveness of the protection circuit is verified.

articleTitle: Intrinsic Polarization in Polarimetrically Beamformed Arrays with Differentially Rotated Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Prior characterization of the sub-systems of a radio telescope which also works as a radio polarimeter is essential in view of the polarimetric performance understanding and the implementation of the most appropriate calibration procedure. In this paper the polarimetric characterization of two phased antenna arrays having identical antennas and array factors but different antenna alignment will be discussed. These arrays have been proposed as possible layouts in the SKA-Low framework. The polarimetric beamforming, i.e. the beamforming for dual-polarized antennas, has been applied to calculate the polarization purity of the two arrays across the sky. In particular we investigated the variation of instrumental polarization along azimuthal cuts and found that the variation was less in the array in which elements had different alignments compared to the one where all elements had the same alignment.

articleTitle: The DSX Mission – Preliminary Results and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Despite many theoretical analyses over the years, the efficiency of VLF radiation from a dipole antenna immersed in a magnetoplasma is poorly understood and not well characterized. This renders the potential effectiveness of “radiation belt remediation” and other aspects of active control highly uncertain. To address this with an “active experiment,” the US Air Force launched and operated the Demonstrations and Science Experiment (DSX) satellite from August 2019 to May 2021, completing over 3,000 orbits lying mostly within the plasmasphere (perigee of 6000 km, apogee of 12000 km, 42 degree inclination) [1]. Its primary focus was attempting active transmission of VLF waves, from a 80-meter (tip-to-tip) dipole antenna. Over 1300 transmissions were attempted, resulting in 78 return signals being received [2], as well as one documented instance of remote reception by the Arase satellite [3, 4].

articleTitle: Digital Pancharatnam-Berry Metasurfaces with 1-bit OAM-Modules for Broadband RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Digital Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) metasurfaces (MSs) with generation of orbital angular momentum (OAM) for RCS reduction (RCSR) are studied. The metasurfaces consist of digital anti-phase 1-bit OAM modules, which contain meta-particles in the form of triple coupled split-ring resonators. A distinctive feature of the OAM modules with a helical profile of the PB-phase is 1-bit coding of the initial meta-particle inclination angle of 45° and 135°. Two mechanisms of RCSR of digital MSs are examined. The one is with the help of generation of vortex beams and other is with the help of phase cancellation of vortex beams. The scattering diagrams of modules and the generation of anti-phase vortex beams with first-order OAM for normally incident circular-polarized waves are studied. The simulation showed that the vortex character of the scattered co-polarized field is preserved in a wide frequency range of 9-21 GHz. The RCSR of two PB-metasurfaces in the form of lattices of in-phase or anti-phase 1-bit OAM modules is investigated.

articleTitle: Emissive probes for plasma diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Cold plasma probes are well established diagnostic tools. They are not complicated, relatively easy to construct and to handle. The easiest and fastest accessible parameter is their floating potential $V_{ff}$. However, $V_{f}$ of a cold probe is not very significant, since in most types of plasmas, consisting mainly of electrons and only positive ions, the floating potential is more negative than the plasma potential $\Phi_{pl}$ by a factor proportional to the electron temperature $T_{e}$. Obviously, this is due to the much higher mobility of the electrons.

articleTitle: A laboratory investigation of Alfvén waves in an Alfvén speed gradient
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Alfvén waves are important in many astrophysical and laboratory plasmas with complex inhomogeneous magnetic structures, such as the solar corona and the Earth’s magnetosphere [1]. Investigating Alfvén waves traveling through such inhomogeneous plasmas is essential for understanding turbulence, damping [2], and heating [3]. In theory, the Alfvén wave is predicted to reflect from the Alfvén speed gradient. In a recent laboratory experiment [4], it was observed that kinetic Alfvén waves (electron thermal speed >> Alfvén speed) lose energy while propagating through the Alfvén speed gradient. But, interestingly, no reflection was observed. We are studying the behavior of inertial Alfvén waves (electron thermal speed << Alfvén speed) as they propagate through the Alfvén speed gradients in the laboratory. We have performed a series of experiments at the Large Plasma Device [5] (LAPD) at the University of California, Los Angeles, to measure the reflection and transmission of inertial Alfvén waves through a gradient parallel to the background magnetic field. The inhomogeneity was created by varying the magnetic field in the direction of the propagation of the Alfvén wave. The Alfvén waves were excited using a loop antenna with multiple wave frequencies below the ion cyclotron frequency. We have observed the reflection of inertial Alfvén waves as they propagate through these Alfvén speed gradients. We will present the results of these experiments.

articleTitle: Accurate Shallow-Buried Object Detection Using Bistatic Drone-Mounted Ground Penetrating Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper shows a study of possible scenarios of using bistatic drone-mounted ground penetrating radar configuration for an accurate shallow-buried object detection. Objects of interest are anti-personnel landmines, which are often made of plastic, with a small amount of metal parts. Because of payload limitations, the system must be small, lightweight and highly efficient. The system is intended in a microwave range of 0.6 GHz-2.6 GHz. Signal reflections are recorded in frequency domain which correlates to Stepped Frequency Continuous Wave measurements and processed through Inverse Fast Fourier Transformation for time domain analysis. Recording in multiple spatial positions enables B-scans generation for object detection. Polarimetric approach and its effects on target detection accuracy will be investigated in the paper.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Vivaldi Antennas for GPR Systems and the Impact of Group Delay.
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The use of Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) systems has emerged as an effective method for detecting landmines, given their ability to detect buried targets, including improvised explosive devices (IEDs), The quality of the measured signal, which is influenced by the antenna, plays a vital role in determining the depth of penetration, resolution, and target detection. [1, 2].

articleTitle: Upper-hybrid waves and fluctuations in space plasma
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Quasi electrostatic fluctuations in the upper-hybrid frequency range are commonly detected in the planetary magnetospheric environment. The origin of such phenomena may relate to the instability driven by a loss-cone feature associated with the electrons populating the dipole-like magnetic field. The present paper carries out a one-dimensional electrostatic particle-in-cell simulation accompanied by a reduced quasilinear kinetic theoretical analysis to investigate the dynamics of the upper-hybrid mode instability driven by an initial ring electron distribution function, which is a form of loss-cone distribution. A favorable comparison is found between the two approaches, which shows that the quasilinear theory can be an effective tool in the study of plasma instabilities, especially if it is guided by, and validated against, the more rigorous simulation result.

articleTitle: Modeling objects with multilayered coatings with High Order Impedance Boundary Condition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper deals with the use of High Order Impedance boundary condition (HOIBC) in 3DMoM codes to improve the accuracy of the Standard Impedance Boundary Condition (SIBC) when modeling multilayer coatings. HOIBC formulation for 3DMoM codes has been presented in [1–3], together with validations. In this paper, we give validations of the HOIBC for multilayered coatings that show the improvement in accuracy obtained over SIBC computations.

articleTitle: Method for Evaluating the Accuracy of Sommerfeld Integrals Calculations in Half-Space Problems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: For the past 100 years, there has been continued interest in simulating antenna and scatterering scenarios above and inside the real ground [1]. Last 50 years the main focus is on fast and accurate numerical evaluation of Sommerfeld integrals, including the recent research looking for solutions of largescale EM problems [2]. Although there are many papers offering various methods for numerical evaluation of Sommerfeld integrals it is challenging task not only to develop a code that performs this numerical evaluation, but also to verify the accuracy of the results. One way to perform such verification is to compare the results with those given in open literature. However, the number of examples available for comparison is limited, and accuracy of presented results is up to some level questionable.

articleTitle: Multi-Screen Boundary Element Methods for the Time Domain Electric Field Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The design of many moderns devices contains conducting multi-screens, i.e. metallic constructs made up from three or more surfaces that meet at so-called junctions. Notable examples are via-holes in high frequency printed circuit boards and integrated chips.

articleTitle: High latitude L-band amplitude scintillation from February 2023 G3 storm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: On February 26<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> and 27<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>, 2023, shocks in the solar wind were recorded near Earth following an M3.7 and an M6.3 solar flares, perturbing the space weather conditions. This was the first and weakest of three major geomagnetic storms of strength G3 and G4 that perturbed the Geospace environment between February and April 2023.

articleTitle: Design of Flexible Simulation Platform for Ignition Control System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: High-power electrical equipment and low-power signal equipment are integrated into the vehicle to form a complex electromagnetic environment. The ignition control signal will be affected in the transmission process, resulting in signal distortion, which threatens the performance and safety of the ignition system. Because the equipment in the car is closely connected with each other, it is not convenient to disassemble, which poses a challenge to the research of the sensitivity of the ignition control system. In this paper, virtual simulation technology is introduced, and the flexible simulation platform of ignition control system is designed by using LabVIEW, which can be used to analyze the disturbance of ignition control system.

articleTitle: UNCD-Armoured Probes for Diagnostics in Hot and Hazardous Plasmas
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Plasma probes are simple and inexpensive diagnostic tools which now are used even in hot and hazardous plasmas, where, however, especially the probe casings, often consisting of graphite, might suffer from sputtering, evaporation and chemical reactions between plasma particles and the probe material. An additional detrimental effect frequently detected is that the sputtered-off electrically conductive graphite re-deposits on the boron nitride material usually used for electrical isolation of the probe pins, leading to unwanted and possibly dangerous shunts to ground and/or to adjacent probes, or even short circuits.

articleTitle: A hybrid analytical-numerical approach for the calculation of the GTD diffraction coefficient for the diffraction at the tip of an arbitrary section cone
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper we present a study whose final goal is the calculation of the diffraction coefficient for rays diffracted at the tip of cones of arbitrary section (including pyramids and angular sectors), in the framework of the Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (GTD) [1]. Following the approach presented in [2], by introducing a spherical reference system with origin at the con tip and by separating the radial coordinate from the angular coordinates, the diffraction coefficient (i.e., the cone scattered field in the plane wave -far field regime) is cast in the Watson integral representation form

articleTitle: MLFMA-slotFFT for the electromagnetic solution of densely packed finite periodic structures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The electromagnetic behavior of periodic structures has gained great interest in recent years due to their fundamental role in the development of scattering networks, plasmonic crystals and many other fields related to nanophotonics, including nanoscale and metasurface devices. Linked to this interest is an increasing demand for the development of tools capable of modelling the electromagnetic behaviour of periodic structures as efficiently as possible. In the context of surface integral equation (SIE) methods based on the method of moments (MoM), most of the existing literature has focused on the development of techniques based on the Ewald method, which requires modelling the system with an infinite periodic structure or dealing with complex physical issues to correctly model the edge effects or the standing waves, whose accurate prediction can be critical in some applications.

articleTitle: Ground VLF transmitter wave propagation in the upper atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Large and powerful ground-based very low frequency (VLF) transmitters, which operate from 17 kHz to 25 kHz with power ranging from several 100s to 1000 kilo-Watts, have been utilized for maintaining long distance communication with submarines for decades dating back to the era before World War I. The transmitters at various locations are often denoted by three letter call sign of Naval VLF transmitter, according to their locations, such as NWC for North West Cape. The long distance communication is realized by VLF wave propagation in the waveguide mode between the Earth and the ionosphere (100-1000 km altitude), which is the lower portion of the ionized upper atmosphere. A fraction of the radio wave power can leak through the ionosphere into the near-Earth geospace environment known as the magnetosphere (~1000 km and above), where VLF signals propagate in the whistler-mode. In the ionosphere, VLF transmitter emissions can cause ionospheric perturbations, particle precipitation and heating. In the inner magnetosphere, VLF transmitter waves can resonate with energetic electrons and contribute to the loss of energetic electrons in radiation belts.

articleTitle: Stochastic Modeling of the Radiation Pattern of Airborne Antennas: Application to the Radar Altimeter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Aircraft include several radio-frequency systems, providing services such as communication, navigation and surveillance. Frequency wise, these systems must coexist with aviation and non-aviation systems, congesting the spectrum. As entry points for any signal, antenna models are key elements for assessing interference risks, as well as external threats. This justifies the need to accurately characterize such antenna radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Interpolation-operator orthogonal, hierarchical H1-conforming basis functions for tetrahedral finite elements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A new $H^{1}$-conforming finite-element basis is proposed. The basis functions are hierarchical in terms of the polynomial order and feature symmetries in terms of barycentric coordinates. The corresponding element matrices exhibit high levels of sparsity and moderate condition numbers in the higher-order case. Moreover, the basis functions are pairwise orthogonal with respect to the finite-element interpolation operator, which is given in explicit form. Thus, the basis possesses not only hierarchical but also interpolatory properties. The resulting interpolation scheme is efficient because it requires the evaluation of only a single scalar product per basis function. An example is presented, where the proposed interpolation scheme is used to construct inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. The numerical results confirm that interpolation yields the same asyptotic rate of convergence as $L^{2}$ approximation, which is much more expensive.

articleTitle: A 2-bit Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface with Filtering Function
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Recently, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) are attracting tremendous interests from wireless community due to their capabilities to manipulate the wireless channel flexibly and rapidly <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>. By building intelligent and controllable wireless environment, RIS could bring a new paradigm to future mobile communication networks with advantages of low cost, low power consumption, and easy deployment.

articleTitle: Analytically Regularized TE-scattering from Ensembles of Slotted Cylinders
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Scattering of electromagnetic waves by an ensemble or cluster of infinitely long, perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) cylinders of arbitrary cross-section has many current and potential applications. Transmission lines, cable bundles and similar structures provide examples where modelling by closely coupled closed cylinders is relevant; determination of the properties of closely coupled slotted cylinders (i.e., with a cavity-backed aperture) possessing sub-wavelength structures underpins the design of metamaterials for use as absorbers and band-pass devices or wave-guiding structures. Determination of the radar cross-section of larger ensembles of cylinders, either open or closed, underpins (particularly in the resonance region) target identification algorithms when the contribution from such ensembles dominates the scattering response.

articleTitle: Integration of Vegetation and Topography Models for GNSS-R
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Various electromagnetic scattering models have been developed for reflections of signals of opportunity (SoOp), such as global navigation satellite system (GNSS) signals, from land surfaces with vegetation cover. These include models that treat vegetation solely as an attenuating layer [1, 2] and those that include provisions of both specular and diffuse scattering using the distorted Born approximation and radiative transfer theory [3–5]. More recently, fast hybrid methods are being developed to compute the transmissivity of vegetation layers using a combination of full-wave numerical solvers and the Foldy-Lax equations for multiple scattering [6].

articleTitle: Deep Generative Regression Models For Soil Moisture Retrieval From GNSS-R Observations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Soil moisture content (SMC) is a crucial component in both the water and carbon cycles, significantly influencing weather and climate. Over recent years, numerous remote sensing platforms have been established to track soil moisture. Leading missions, such as NASA’s SMAP and the ESA’s SMOS, offer global-scale coarse-resolution soil moisture monitoring using active and passive microwave imaging at a moderate revisit frequency on the scale of days. Regrettably, current products’ spatial and temporal resolution is often insufficient for many applications. Global navigation satellite system reflectometry (GNSS-R) is a prime example of a signal-of-opportunity (SoOP) which has been shown to be highly sensitive variations of SMC. An important source of such signals is the NASA Cyclone GNSS (CYGNSS) mission which consists of eight low-orbit observatories, each utilizing a zenith antenna to receive direct global positioning system (GPS) signals, as well as two nadir-looking antennas to receive reflected GPS signals, that are used to derive a delay-Doppler map (DDM). In order to extract SMC from DDM signals, the traditional approach involves inverting parameterized forward models which account for aspects like dielectric properties of the soil incidence angle among others. Despite their grounding in physical processes, these models typically involve simplified assumptions and demonstrate increased sensitivity to the values of different parameters. To address this challenge, a new line of research tries to address this challenge by utilizing machine learning models and treating the problem as that of supervised regression e.g.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>.

articleTitle: Electron Thermal Anisotropy During Electron-Only Reconnection in PHASMA
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A regime of reconnection, called electron-only reconnection since there is insufficient time or space for ions to couple with reconnection structures, provides an opportunity to study electron heating mechanisms more directly than in fully ion-coupled reconnection. Electron-only reconnection is thought to be important for energy dissipation at kinetic scales in Earth’s turbulent magnetosheath, bow shock and the quiet magnetotail. Recent simulations of turbulent near-Sun plasmas suggest that electron-only reconnection with a large guide field plays a key role in the dissipation of turbulent energy at the kinetic scale and results in parallel, i.e. anisotropic, electron heating.

articleTitle: Recent High Power Electromagnetics Research at the University of New Mexico
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Research in high power electromagnetics at the University of New Mexico ranges from advancing the state-of-the-art in high power microwave devices from L-band to E-band, developing novel high power microwave antennas, to studying the electromagnetic compatibility issue of devices to high power electromagnetic interference.

articleTitle: Test Methods for Natural and Stimulated Emissions in the Ionosphere and Magnetosphere
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Air Force Office of Scientific Research’s (AFOSR) mission is to support United States Air Force goals of maximum utilization of air and space. AFOSR accomplishes its mission by investing in basic research efforts for the Department of the Air Force and Space Force in relevant scientific areas. The region between 40 km – 1000 km in altitude is a relevant space domain offering fundamental science challenges to measure stimulated and natural emissions. Space Shuttle entry tracks [1] from 160 km to 40 km delineate the complexity the region; particularly Space Transportation System-4 which hit a “pothole in-the-sky.” Value of precise test measurement in the ionosphere region and magnetosphere includes characterization of chemistry non-equilibrium properties and exploration of non-linear plasma physics.

articleTitle: Cross-field structure generation approaching dissipation scales via three-wave coupling of shear Alfvén waves and kink waves
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Both kink waves (arising from unstable magnetic flux ropes) and shear Alfvén waves occur simultaneously in plasmas ranging from solar prominences, the solar wind, magnetic fusion devices, and Earth’s magnetotail. The potential interaction between these typically large-scale phenomena leading to smaller cross-field scales and eventually dissipation in these domains could thus be of broad interest.

articleTitle: A Direct Solver Based on Generalized Debye Sources for Electromagnetic Scattering
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A fast direct solver based on the generalized Debye sources for problems of electromagnetic scattering by conducting bodies has been developed. The fields are represented via two vector and two scalar potentials, which, in turn, are expressed via two fictitious charge densities. This approach reduces to simultaneously solving two Fredholm integral equations for scalar quantities and two Poisson’s equations with the surface Laplacian. It is free from spurious resonances and the low-frequency breakdown. The proposed generalized Debye sources-based direct solver uses the hierarchical interpolation grids of the multilevel non-uniform grid (MLNG) algorithm and a rank-revealing solution scheme.

articleTitle: Inverse Estimation of Electron Trajectory from Liénard-Wiechert Vortex Fields
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Since L.Allen pointed out in 1992 that the Laguerre-Gaussian laser beam carries well-defined orbital angular momentum [1] in addition to linear and spin angular momentum, the optical vortex have been investigated actively not only from scientific viewpoints but also industry applications such as large capacity optical fiber communication.
