articleTitle: Array Analysis by Iterative Localised Solutions with Improved Convergence
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The method of moments (MoM) is well-suited to radiation and scattering analysis of array structures. Domain decomposition strategies for array analysis, where only successive localised solutions are required to converge to the global solution, can yield high computational efficiency. Recently, such an iterative scheme has been proposed, which is denoted the direct coupling technique (DCT). In this paper, an extension to the DCT scheme is discussed, which is shown to improve its convergence. The scheme is suitable for large-scale parallelisation.

articleTitle: High μ core ELF/VLF Miro-Array Transmitters (MAT) for Space Platforms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: ELF/VLF waves with frequencies from few Hz to several kHz are a ubiquitous component of the ionosphere, the near-Earth magnetosphere, and the Radiation Belts (RB). They are generated by instabilities, lightning discharges, and ground VLF transmitters. Observations by the Van-Allen probes confirmed the role of nonlinear interactions driven by anthropogenic VLF sources in controlling space weather phenomena and the population of MeV electrons in the Radiation Belts (RB). The MeV electrons are known as “killer electrons” due to their adverse effects on the operation and lifetime of LEO communications and reconnaissance satellites. However, despite their importance their properties and especially their non-linear interaction has never been tested in space. This is due to the inefficiency of conventional electric and magnetic dipole transmitters. In experiments at the UCLA LAPD chamber, we tested a Rotating Magnetic Field (RMF) as an antenna. The RMF consisted of two orthogonal coils with magnetic moment (M) perpendicular to the B field, driven by AC currents with phase difference ± π/2, and frequency to drive RH Whistlers above the ion cyclotron frequency (Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>) and LH Electro-Magnetic Ion Cyclotron (EMIC) below Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>. It was found<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> that contrary to the ELF/VLF dipoles the RMF waves had helical phase surfaces described by Exp(±mϕ+kz-ωt). The magnetic topology is a combination of a loop with M ⊥ B, that propagates along B while rotating about it. The combination of phase rotation and translation results in spiraling phase surfaces like Helicons<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (H). RMF antennae: (i) Introduce Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) much larger that due to polarization; (ii) Control the radial wavenumber ±m; (iii) The antenna determines the transverse phase and amplitude profile while the highly aligned group velocity (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>) prevents radial energy spread; (iv) Generates large OAM and large k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</inf> that result in large transverse magnetic field gradients and transverse Doppler shifts of energetic electrons with rotating waves that facilitate breaking the adiabatic invariance of the “killer electrons”, as verified in LAPD experiments<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The drawback of the RMF antenna was its low radiation resistance. The LAPD experiments utilized loops with 8 cm diameter, driven by 600 A each, resulting in M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</inf>= 11.5 A-m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and generated power P=250 W. The resulting radiation resistance was R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>=2x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> Ohm. A value very low to generate B field amplitude exceeding the threshold for non-linear wave-particle interactions that result in triggering<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> of Whistlers and EMIC waves. In LAPD experiments<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> and current experiments in the NRL chamber we introduced a novel type of antenna the consisting of a long solenoid with small diameter d=O(cm) and aspect ratio larger than 30, into which a core of a non-conducting high μ material was inserted. The first set of experiments used a Ferrite Loop Antenna (FLA) in which a high μ ferrite was inserted in the solenoid. The experiments demonstrated that phasing individual FLA rods with their M perpendicular to B reproduced all the helicon properties of the RFM properties mentioned previously. It was further demonstrated that that radiation resistance contributed by each rod R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>(μ)=μ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>R(μ=l). Both RH W/H and LH EMIC/H waves were driven. Using a two element anti-phased array FLA rods perpendicular to B resulted in m=±1 H-modes like those driven by the RMF. Using ferrite with μ=30 the two-element array driven by I=1.6 A had M=10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> A-m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>and generated power P=.34 W. The measured R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>=.14 Ohm was more than 30 dB higher than the RMF under similar plasma parameters. Control of k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</inf> by using ten-element phase-array and controlling the angle of the array with respect to B. Examples of radially and azimuthally phased arrays will be presented. The presentation will conclude with the first proof of principle experiments of the Magnetic Nano-Transmitter<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> (MNT). The MNT is a phased array whose elements are in which the core of the solenoid is filled by superparamagnetic nanoparticles embedded in a non-conducting solid, such as epoxy or paraffin. Theoretical estimates indicate that using a mixture 50%-50% Fe-Co, MNT can achieve performance by more than 20 dB higher than the FLA arrays, and importantly for space-based transmitter achieve it by an order of magnitude lower weight.

articleTitle: On the physics and design of plasmonic anapoles in metallic nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Nanostructures with anapole states have attracted significant interest in the field of nanophotonics due to their ability to exhibit field enhancement while providing transparency, specifically a low extinction cross-section [1, 2]. Anapoles have been observed in both dielectric [3] and plasmonic [4] nanostructures. Typically, anapole states arise from the interference between electric and toroidal dipole moments. However, even in cases where the toroidal dipole contribution is negligible due to a planar design, the presence of an anapole can still be observed.

articleTitle: Modeling and Optimizing Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces in Wireless Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In [1], the authors have recently introduced a circuits-based approach for modeling the mutual coupling of reconfigurable surfaces, which comprise sub-wavelength spaced passive scattering elements coupled with electronic circuits for enabling the reconfiguration of the surface. The approach is based on a finite-length discrete dipole representation of a reconfigurable surface, and on the assumption that the current distribution on each thin wire dipole is a sinusoidal function. Under these assumptions, the voltages at the ports of a multi-antenna receiver can be formulated in terms of the voltage generators at a multi-antenna transmitter through a transfer function matrix that explicitly depends on the mutual coupling and the tuning circuits through the mutual impedances between every pair of thin wire dipoles. In [2] and [3], the authors have proposed optimization methods for application of the model in wireless networks. Finally, in [4], the authors have formulated the mutual impedances in an integral form.

articleTitle: A Novel Intergration Method for Wideband Radar via Mainlobe Broadening
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In order to enhance the extended target detectability, a novel mismatched filter characterized by a forced broadening of the 3 dB mainlobe width (MW) of the output response is designed. Similar to the target energy accumulation of the narrowband radar, the designed filter is able to concentrate the energy of the scattering centers into the same resolution unit. To this end, 3 dB MW, mismatched filter gain, and signal-noise ratio (SNR) constraints are forced on the mismatched filter, while integration sidelobe level (ISL) is taken as the figure of merit to minimize. To handle the resulting non-convex problem, a polynomial-time method based on sequential convex approximation (SCA) which slacks the non-convex constraint is proposed to decrease ISL. Numerical results are provided to show that the 3 dB MW can be successfully broadened in a certain range, and the extended target energy can be accumulated efficiently.

articleTitle: Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces Driven By Reinforcement Learning Controller for 6G Indoor Coverage Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS) are one of the most exciting and innovative technologies for improving the power and spectral efficiency of wireless systems. These devices can modify the wireless propagation environment by setting the phase shifts of large numbers of inexpensive passive reflective elements. This paper aims to show the potential and limitations of IRS driven by a Reinforcement Learning Controller in particularly though indoor environments, where it is too expensive or even structurally unfeasible to lay cables, for the implementation of Distributed Antenna Systems (DAS).

articleTitle: Initial Concept and Roadmap of the Band-4+5 Receiver Upgrade of the Atacama Large Millimeter / Submillimeter Array (ALMA)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Band-4+5 receivers of the Atacama Large Millimeter / Submillimeter Array (ALMA) is proposed for the upgrade after 2030. The new receiver will cover the RF frequency of the original Band-4 (125 – 163 GHz) and Band-5 (163 -211 GHz) with continuous frequency tuning over dual polarizations, dual sidebands with instantaneous intermediate frequency (IF) bandwidth up to 16 GHz per sideband and per polarization.

articleTitle: Estimation of Electromagnetic Absorption Characteristics Using a Human Model with Anatomical Structures at Frequencies above 100 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Beyond 5G/6G, which is currently under development, envisages the use of radio waves up to the terahertz band above 300 GHz. However, the detailed human exposure characteristics in the frequency range expected to be used in Beyond 5G/6G above 100 GHz are not clear. As the frequency increases, the absorption coefficient of water molecules increases, and radio waves are absorbed in shallower parts of the human body. In the terahertz band, electromagnetic absorption occurs in very shallow parts of the body surface (skin and eyeballs). Therefore, in this study, we estimated the electromagnetic field exposure to an eyeball at 100 GHz to 300 GHz by large-scale numerical simulation using an ultra-high-resolution computational human model with anatomical structures that we have developed previously. A graphics processing unit (GPU) cluster system (with approximately 3.8T of available GPU memory) equipped with the latest GPU (Nvidia Tesla A100) was built to perform the numerical simulation. A full-scratch finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) code for GPU cluster computations was used to efficiently run the numerical simulations on the GPU cluster system [1]. In this study, a half-wavelength dipole antenna (output power 1 W) was placed 20 mm in front of the eye of a computational human model (Japanese adult male model: TARO [2]) with a resolution of approximately 0.03 mm and the SAR was calculated as shown in Fig. 1 (a). As the resolution of the computational human model was set to 0.03 mm, a part of the head was cut out and used in this calculation, taking into account the amount of GPU memory on our GPU cluster system. As a result, electromagnetic energy in the frequency band above 100 GHz is absorbed only in very shallow areas of the human body surface as shown in Fig. 1 (b), and absorption of electromagnetic energy (e.g. the average specific absorption rate (SAR) in the lens is less than 0.0001 W/kg) is negligible in areas a few millimeters deep from the body surface. On the other hand, the subdivision and detailing of the body surface tissues is important for a highly accurate estimation of exposure above 100 GHz. Temperature rise was also estimated using the SAR as a heat source. A 0.03mm resolution model was downconverted and a 1mm resolution model was used to estimate the temperature rise; as with SAR, the SAR-induced temperature rise was concentrated on a very shallow part of the body surface. In this presentation, human exposure characteristics from 100 GHz to 300 GHz will be demonstrated in detail.

articleTitle: Investigation of Pivoting Strategies for the Application of the Adaptive Cross Approximation to the Magnetic Field Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Integral equations such as the electric field integral equation (EFIE), magnetic field integral equation (MFIE), or combined field integral equation (CFIE) are a popular choice to solve electromagnetic scattering and radiation problems. Standard discretizations via the boundary element method (BEM) lead, however, to dense matrices. Compressed with techniques such as the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) or the adaptive cross approximation (ACA), the cost of a single matrix-vector product can be reduced to quasi-linear complexity [1]. An advantage of the ACA is that the algorithm is purely algebraic. Therefore, the ACA is applicable in a blackbox-like manner to system matrices arising from integral equations where the integral kernel is asymptotically smooth and when a global pivoting strategy is used [2].

articleTitle: Discrete Taylor Transform and Inverse Transform of Univariate Functions on Nonuniform Lattices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Discrete Taylor Transform and Inverse Transform (D-TTIT) of univariate functions on uniform grids was proposed by this author in 2020-2021. The theory was extended in 2022-2023 to include bivariate and trivariate functions. The theory of frames underlies the conception of D-TTIT. This paper presents a further extension of the theory to permit functions on nonuniform lattices. Details are illustrated by a toy model consisting of five monomials, the discretization of which constitutes the frame vectors. Subsequently, the associated frame operator is built, which in turn leads to the formation of dual frames (higher-order derivative operators). The constructed frame and dual frames jointly resolve the identity operator and are mutually biorthonormal. D-TTIT provides a universal and flexible handle on the construction of derivative stencils on uniform, nonuniform, or randomly distributed lattice points in multi-dimensions. This paper focuses on the nonuniformity of grid points and the implications thereof.

articleTitle: 3D Mapping of Surface Profiles by Radar Measurements at E-Band Employing On-Site Near-Field Calibration
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: For many applications it is essential to know the exact information about a surface profile or a soil level. For this purpose, a very irregular surface is created with sand, and its surface profile is measured with the aid of a 4-D E-band radar sensor employing a total number of more than 1700 channels. Typically, high-precision in-situ calibrations are employed to ensure the best possible radar performance. Unfortunately, environmental influences, such as the temperature, vary strongly between the initial calibration scenario and the application scenario, making a re-calibration necessary. To ensure the proper operation of the sensor a re-calibration is performed at the exact time and location of application. To be independent of the scene under investigation, the calibration target is placed in the near-field of the sensor and out of the main lobe illuminating the area under test. Furthermore, the calibration in field-trials is performed by means of a calibration target without the need for a precise mechanical placement. Therefore, a highly precise in-situ calibration is used to estimate the position of the calibration target. A field-trial is deployed to show the radar performance with on-site near-field calibration and a comparison to an initial calibration in the far-field of the radar sensor is conducted to demonstrate the compensation of near-field effects on the calibration.

articleTitle: Beam-Steering Antennas Using Semi-Periodic Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Metasurfaces advance the technology to develop high-performance antenna systems due to their unique electromagnetic (EM) wave manipulation capabilities. This article describes the antenna beam-steering mechanism using semiperiodic metasurfaces (locally aperiodic metasurfaces). Metasurfaces are synthesized based on the near-field phase transformation principle and placed atop the fixed-beam antenna to steer the beam dynamically, following Risley prism techniques. We discuss several advances that have been made since the technology was first introduced.

articleTitle: Investigation of System Distortions by Scattering of Very Large Wind-Turbines in Some Distance to DME-Navigation Stations on the Ground
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper describes the application of the numerical 3D-modelling and scattering analysis for the multiscatterer case, such as for wind-farms (WF) related to a pulse based DME-system (Distance Measuring Equipment). The resulting DME-range-error is affected by pulse-distortions by scattering of large wind-turbines (WTs) in some distance to the DME-ground-station. The DME-system, the generation and aspects of range errors and some numerical simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: Characteristics of electron microburst precipitation: probing wave-particle interactions in Earth’s magnetosphere
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Whistler-mode chorus waves, frequently observed in Earth’s magnetosphere, scatter energetic electrons into the atmosphere over a wide energy range $(0.1keV-\gt1MeV)$, producing the diffuse and pulsating aurora, and electron microbursts. Microbursts are intense, short ($\sim 100$ ms) bursts of precipitating electrons. They were first detected between $10-100keV$ using balloon-based instrumentation [1], and subsequently shown to extend to relativistic energies. Microbursts occur in quasi-periodic or pulsating groups and their association with whistler-mode chorus was first established by [2]. $\gt1 MeV$ electrons are thought to interact through higher-order resonance or off-equatorial interactions [3]. Although, this association is well accepted, details about the wave-particle interactions are not well understood. Since the discovery of very large amplitude whistler-mode waves in the magnetosphere [4], the importance of nonlinear interactions has become a major topic of study.

articleTitle: Efficient Evaluation of Test Integrals for Surface Method of Moments Based on Vertex Functions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The performance of any surface integral equations (SIE) code developed using the method of moments (MoM) is based on the efficient evaluation of a double surface integral. Much effort has been focused on the efficient solution of the interior (source) integral [1–2]. However, improving the exterior (test) integral is usually ignored, it often being assumed that once the inner integral has been evaluated, the integrand of the outer integral is sufficiently smooth that it may be evaluated numerically using standard numerical integration. However, this assumption is not always valid. As shown in [3], the evaluation of the outer integrals can be inefficient and surprisingly inaccurate, especially for dominant reactions such as between edge-and vertex-adjacent test and source triangles or for poorly-shaped triangles.

articleTitle: Development of diffraction electronics in IRE NAS of Ukraine
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: S. Smith and E. Purcell where the first who observed optical radiation of electrons moving over diffraction grating [1]. Only in 10 years after that seminal experiment, the first theoretical work on the theory of the Smith-Purcell radiation, or Diffraction Radiation Effect was reported at the $3^{rd}$ All-Union Symposium on Wave Diffraction (Tbilisi, September 1963) [2]. In more detail, the obtained results were published one year later in the $7^{th}$ Issue of the "Radio Engineering and Electronics" journal in the paper "Radiation of electromagnetic waves by an electron beam moving over a diffraction grating" (O.A. Tretyakov, S.S. Tretyakova, and V.P. Shestopalov) [3]. The authors pointed to the possibility of using the diffraction radiation to produce EM waves either by modulated electron beam or by short bunches of electrons flying over the periodic structure. Though in this work the creation of a self-oscillator was not discussed, nevertheless, the authors already then thought about the implementation of this effect in the microwave range, proposing to obtain a modulated electron beam with the help of a photocathode irradiated by superposition of two lasers beams with different frequencies, which provided modulation of the photocurrent at the difference frequency. Further, as far as we know, professor Victor P. Shestopalov has made multiple attempts to attract experts in the field of microwave electronics to design a new millimeter-wave generator, based on the diffraction radiation. However, he had to arrange this research himself with essential support by Olexandr Usikov, Director of the IRE NASU, Kharkiv. As a result, a new research area in millimeter and sub-millimeter wave (THz) vacuum electronics was founded by Victor Shestopalov in IRE NASU, and it has been under intense research and development during the following 35 years under his leadership. In the Victor P. Shestopalov School, the very effect of diffraction radiation (Smith-Purcell radiation), i.e., the bulk radiation of a charge moving near the diffraction grating surface, was considered as the main physical effect necessary to create an oscillator on bulk wave feedback, but not on surface ones. The provision of feedback and the choice of an oscillatory system had to follow from the features and patterns of this radiation, from the electromagnetic laws and the excitation theory of OR. The next step might be a theory of related self-oscillatory system. That is why a new device was named as Diffraction Radiation Oscillator (DRO). The DRO study has been carried out theoretically, experimentally and technologically. The goals of the research were both in-depth understanding of the physical phenomena occurring in DRO and the developing of the devices which should meet requirements of various applications in millimeter and submillimeter wavelength ranges (35-500 GHz).

articleTitle: Radiating and guided scattering emerging at temporal interfaces in time-varying metamaterials and guiding structures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Metamaterials and metasurfaces are currently a key-enabling technology for achieving unprecedented control of the wave propagation and new anomalous scattering effects. In the last few years, the possibilities offered by metamaterials have been further extended thanks to the exploitation of the time dimension as degree of freedom for designing novel metastructures [1] or achieving new scattering phenomena, such as virtual absorption [2–3], Doppler cloaking [4], and efficient phase-conjugation in leaky waveguides [5] In this framework, temporal metamaterials is a class of artificial media whose electromagnetic properties changes in step-like fashion, enabling novel radiating and guided scattering effects, such as reflectionless and lasing [6], generation of effective media in time domain [7], and temporal Brewster angle propagation [8], and efficient phase-conjugation for leaky waveguides [9].

articleTitle: Exact calculation of matrix entries in space-time Galerkin time domain boundary element method for the scalar wave equation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The contribution of this work is to propose an exact calculation for the interaction elements appearing in space-time time domain boundary element methods based on a dimensionality reduction procedure. Similar methods have been applied in the frequency domain, while in the time domain only numerical or semi-analytical approaches have been proposed. The calculation presented here replaces a four dimensional interaction integral with a sum of lower dimensional integrals of a new effective Green function that can be evaluated in closed form. In this paper the method proposed is applied to scalar basis an testing function on flat supports but it can be adapted to the electromagnetic case. The results can be used as a benchmark to evaluate the precision and stability of existing numerical methods. It allows to distinguish instabilities inherent to the method and those that appear as a consequence of limited quadrature precision.

articleTitle: Comparison of Different Electromagnetic Delay Lines for X-Band Radar Target Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, two different types of electromagnetic delay lines for radar testing applications are presented. The structures are evaluated with regards to their properties for radar target generation, these features being the velocity factor, signal attenuation, dispersion and bandwidth. The delay lines shall be complemented with attenuators and filters to approximate an authentic free space target. Next to fundamentals and simulation results, several measurements and different use cases are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Reservoir Water Storage Level Monitoring Using CYGNSS’s Spaceborne GNSS-R Constellation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Water supply management and forecasting applications motivate the production of near-real time estimates of water levels and extents on spatial scales ranging from the local to the global. Spaceborne remote sensing is of interest for this purpose provided that sufficient revisit times and coverage are achieved. Global Navigation Satellite System-Reflectometry (GNSS-R) systems can be advantageous in this application due to the modest cost of an observatory that can allow the simultaneous launch of multiple receivers, thereby reducing revisit times. The L-band microwave frequency used in GNSS-R also allows penetration through vegetation canopies while remaining unaffected by cloud cover and precipitation. The spatial resolutions achieved, which can be as fine as ~150 meters in some cases, also can be sufficient in the monitoring of larger water reservoirs.

articleTitle: Position estimation using the loop antenna in the sea
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: When divers rescue people who have accidents at sea, they are in a hazardous environment. If they can confirm their positions, their activities will be conducted more safely and reliably. In this research, we propose an undersea positioning technology using electromagnetic waves with low frequencies. In this report, we consider position estimation using the loop antenna in the sea using a pseudo-scale model.

articleTitle: Development of Thermal Rehabilitation System for Simultaneous Heating of Both Knees
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper describes the development of a heating system for the deep thermal rehabilitation of knees. Osteoarthritis is more common in elderly people, as the aging population increase, the number of patients tends to increase every year. Hyperthermia is one of the clinical therapies used to treat OA, and it is a clinical fact that heating the knee joint has the effect of relieving pain and suppressing the progression of symptoms. In this study, a new applicator that can heat both knees simultaneously was developed to increase the possibility of clinical application of the resonator heating method. A coupled analysis of the electromagnetic field and temperature distribution using a knee model and a high-resolution whole-body model was carried out to numerically investigate the heating characteristics of the proposed applicator. From the analysis results using the two models, it was confirmed that the applicator could simultaneously heat the targeted internal parts of both knees.

articleTitle: A Simple and Novel Planar Structure to Excite Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper a low-profile and novel planar excitation technique is proposed to excite characteristic modes of a patch antenna. The proposed exciter consists of a printed balun and four exciters are positioned at the middle of each side of a square plate. Rectangular and circular slits are incorporated to each side of the square plate to achieve wide band operation. The designed antenna element operates in 24-31 GHz frequency band with VSWR below 2:1 and four different radiation modes can be obtained by exciting the ports with appropriate phase shifts corresponding to the radiation mode of interest. Simplicity of the designed antenna structure enables the utilization of the antenna element in a massive MIMO base station for 5G mmWave applications.

articleTitle: Helmholtz-Galerkin Technique for the Analysis of the Diffraction from a Resistive-Filled Circular Hole in a Resistive Plane
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, the analysis of the plane-wave diffraction from a resistive-filled circular hole in a resistive plane is formulated in terms of an infinite set of singular dual integral equations in the vector Hankel transform domain. To achieve an approximate solution of the problem, the integral equations are suitably discretized by means of the HelmholtzGalerkin technique, thus leading to fast-converging Fredholm second-kind matrix operator equations in $l^{2}$.

articleTitle: Research on Active Protection Test Verification System against Same Frequency Conducted EMI
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Over the past few years, there has been a growing interest in high-speed maglev trains. The electromagnetic environment surrounding these trains is quite complex. Low frequency EMI is very significant. This disturbance can easily cause interference with the train control equipment, mainly through conducted coupling. This problem can seriously affect the reliability and safety of train operations. The communication signal frequencies used by this equipment are mostly concentrated at kHz. Traditional filtering technology can only eliminate interference signals located outside the signal band. These filtering methods find it difficult to filter out interfering signals in the same-frequency band.

articleTitle: High Modulation Freedom Leaky-wave Antenna Based on Sinusoidal Phase Grating Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Leaky-wave antenna (LWA) is a guiding-wave structure, that gradually radiate electromagnetic wave into free space along its transmission direction [1–3]. An important research component of a LWA is to increase the modulation degrees of freedom. A novel LWA, which can manipulate radiation phase, radiation direction and radiation gain by simply adjusting the structural parameters, is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna is achieved by bending the transmission line along a sinusoidal curve, as shown in equation (1).

articleTitle: Solitons for Orbital Debris Detection and Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Small sized orbital debris objects (<5 cms) are hard to detect optically from ground based instruments and pose a major threat to space assets in the Low Earth Orbit (LEO) and Geosynchronous Orbit (GEO) regions. A novel idea of exploiting plasma effects to provide an indirect means of detecting and tracking such objects was first proposed in 2015 [1]. The basic concept is as follows. Since the debris objects are moving in the ionospheric plasma medium they can get highly charged due to the flow of electron and ion currents on them. As charged objects their motion can create electrostatic and/or electromagnetic wakes in a manner analogous to wakes created by objects moving in a neutral fluid. However, when the object speed exceeds a critical velocity, like the phase speed of a collective mode of the medium, it can excite nonlinear fore-wake structures in the form of solitons that move away from it in the forward direction. Such a phenomenon, that is well known in hydrodynamics [2], was shown to be theoretically possible in plasmas when the speed of the charged object exceeded the ion acoustic velocity [1], a condition that is easily fulfilled by debris objects in the LEO region. Two kinds of solitons were predicted – forward moving precursor solitons and stationary pinned solitons that remained attached to the debris object as an enveloping nonlinear electrostatic structure. The calculated scale sizes and amplitudes of these nonlinear structures were found to be comparable to those of ionospheric irregularities and hence within the detection capabilities of ground based radars or in-situ sensors. It was therefore suggested that these solitons could provide an indirect means of detecting and tracking small sized debris objects. This basic idea was subsequently strengthened and developed in a number of later works. An experimental verification of the existence of precursor solitons was provided in a laboratory experiment where upstreaming dust acoustic solitons were observed when a dusty plasma was made to flow supersonically over a stationary electrostatic potential hill [3]. The experimental results were well validated by model calculations based on a forced Korteweg-de Vries (fKdV) equation [3] as well as fluid and molecular dynamic simulations [4]. The original calculations of [1], were further extended and refined in a detailed feasibility study [5], to work out the amplitude, width, and production frequency of ion acoustic solitons that may be produced by millimeter and centimeter-scale orbital debris as a function of the debris’ size, velocity, and location (altitude, latitude, and longitude) about the Earth. Since electrostatic structures can suffer strong Landau damping in the Low Earth Orbit (LEO) region they can be quite short lived. Electromagnetic nonlinear structures might provide a better alternative by creating longer life time and larger spatial extent solitons. Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations [6] and fluid model studies [7] have delineated the existence regimes and characteristic of such electromagnetic structures. Presently there are efforts to establish their existence in a controlled laboratory experiment in the large plasma device at the Naval Research Laboratory (NRL), U.S.A. More realistic theoretical modeling of the soliton dynamics that accounts for three dimensional effects as well as inhomogeneous wake flow effects are currently in progress. In view of all these developments the concept of soliton detection of debris objects has been identified as an attractive option in the recent IARPA inititiative [8] inviting proposals based on novel techniques for debris detection and tracking.

articleTitle: Broadband Modal Solution of the Full-Wave Method of Moments Based on a Quasi-Static Eigenvalue Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A novel modal solution of the Full-Wave Method of Moments (MoM) based on a quasi-static eigenvalue problem is presented. The resulting modal current solutions have to be determined only once and serve as global basis and test functions. By extracting the static modes from the full-wave system, the system order can be significantly reduced. Furthermore, the modal solution provides also a physical insight into the system behaviour and can therefore, similar to the Characteristic Mode Analysis, be used for EMC optimizations tasks, whereby the eigenvalue problem has to be solved only once. The method is validated by comparison with the conventional Full-Wave MoM as reference.

articleTitle: Phase-gradient metasurfaces for antenna applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Phase-gradient metasurfaces are innovative devices able to mold in an almost arbitrary way the flow of electromagnetic waves [1]–[2]. In the transmission scenario, phase-gradient metasurfaces generally consist of a discrete set of Huygens meta-atoms, either metallic [1] or fully dielectric [3], introducing an engineered phase profile along the transverse direction.

articleTitle: A Novel Low-Scattering Vivaldi Array Design Method by Loading Resistive Reflecting Units
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, a novel low-scattering design method of Vivaldi array antennas is proposed in this paper, i.e., controlling structural mode scattering to cancel antenna mode scattering of the array. To achieve a more complete cancellation in a broad band, resistive reflecting units are elaborately co-designed with Vivaldi elements and loaded at critical positions of array edges. Thus, desired in-band co-polarized monostatic scattering cross section reduction (SCSR) is achieved. An 8 × 8 low-scattering Vivaldi array is calculated to verify the proposed low-scattering method, compared with a referenced array. Calculated results demonstrate the notable broadband SCSR, larger than 20dB compared to the metal ground in X-band, and broadband wide-angle scanning performances of the array are not affected by proposed low-scattering method.
